advancedExpressions.example: I would strongly recommend setting aside a separate lane for cyclists, which would not only ease the congestion at the gate but also protect students from unnecessary risk. （setting aside动名词提建议 + which非限定从句陈述双重好处）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as a runner must stay in his own lane to ..., so must sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as a runner must stay in his own lane to reach the finish, so must each of us follow the path best suited to our talents rather than blindly copying the crowd. （"just as..., so must..."类比句式，以泳道/跑道喻人生道路）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I rode my bike down the lane and felt happy.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I let the bicycle carry me down the sun-dappled lane, the wind combing through my hair and a reckless joy bubbling up inside me, until I could not help but shout my happiness to the indifferent hedgerows. （读后续写·骑行·感官+心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 拟人化让bicycle作主语(let the bicycle carry me) + 环境细节(sun-dappled, hedgerows) + 情绪递进(bubbling up→shout) + 感官描写(wind combing through hair)

sentenceUpgrade.original: The city should build more bicycle lanes.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time that the municipal authorities carved out more dedicated cycling lanes, for such a measure would simultaneously relieve traffic pressure, cut carbon emissions, and encourage a healthier way of life. （议论文·城市规划）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time that + 过去式虚拟语气 + for引导原因 + 三项并列递进(relieve...cut...encourage)展现多重益处

classPractice.question: 厌倦了快节奏的生活，他搬到了乡下。Tired of life in the ____ ____, he moved to the countryside.
classPractice.note: life in the fast lane 快节奏（紧张刺激）的生活，固定短语

classPractice.question: 选词填空(lane / path / alley)：We turned off the main road onto a quiet country ____ fringed with wild flowers.
classPractice.note: 两旁有边界（树篱）的乡间窄路用 lane；path 泛指步行小径，alley 指城中暗巷

classPractice.question: The driver signalled and carefully changed ____ (lane) before the exit.
classPractice.note: change lanes（变换车道）习惯用复数 lanes

translation: 陪同，陪伴；伴随，与……同时发生；为……伴奏
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort
(2) vt. to happen or exist at the same time as something else
(3) vt. to play a musical instrument, especially the piano, while someone else sings or plays the main tune
(4) vt. to provide something in addition to something else

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (为歌唱或独奏)伴奏
uncommonMeanings.example: As her trembling voice rose in the silent hall, her old teacher slipped onto the stool and began to accompany her on the piano, and suddenly she was no longer alone. （读后续写·师生·音乐会）

posExamples.sentence: My grandmother insisted on accompanying me to the station that frosty morning, her arm looped through mine, chatting brightly so that neither of us would have to acknowledge the goodbye drawing near. （读后续写·送别·情感克制）
I would be more than glad to accompany our foreign guests around the campus, introducing them to our library, laboratories and the century-old plane trees of which we are so proud. （应用文·志愿者申请信）
Genuine progress is almost always accompanied by discomfort, for growth demands that we abandon the familiar and venture, however reluctantly, into the unknown. （议论文·成长与代价·观点句）
A sudden hush accompanied the raising of the curtain, and in that breathless silence I could hear my own heart hammering against my ribs. （读后续写·登台·紧张画面）

wordForms.noun: accompaniment (伴奏/伴随物) / accompanist (伴奏者)
wordForms.other: ★拼写与变形：以“辅音字母+y”结尾，第三人称/过去式变 y 为 i → accompanies / accompanied；现在分词直接加 -ing → accompanying。名词伴奏 accompaniment（注意 -ni-）

collocations.phrase: accompany sb (to somewhere) = keep sb company
collocations.example: Who will accompany you to the airport? 谁陪你去机场？（课件·Integrated skills；= keep sb company 陪伴某人）

collocations.phrase: be accompanied by sth (exist at the same time as)
collocations.example: strong winds accompanied by heavy rain 伴有大雨的强风（课件·Integrated skills，义2 伴随）

collocations.translation: 【课件】使某物伴有某物；边……边配以……
collocations.example: He accompanied his speech with gestures. 他边讲边配以手势。（课件·Integrated skills）

collocations.phrase: accompany sb at / on the piano; be accompanied at / on the piano
collocations.example: The singer was accompanied at / on the piano by his pupil. 这位歌唱家由他的学生用钢琴伴奏。（课件·Integrated skills，义3 伴奏）

collocations.translation: 【课件·辨析】陪伴某人（动词 accompany ↔ 名词短语 keep sb company）
collocations.example: I'll accompany you home. = I'll keep you company on the way home. 我陪你回家。（课件·Integrated skills 辨析：company [U] 陪伴／companion [C] 同伴）
My grandmother insisted on accompanying me to the station that frosty morning. （读后续写·送别·陪伴）
Children under twelve must be accompanied by an adult at all times during the visit. （应用文·须知；被动结构，最常考）

collocations.phrase: accompany sb. on the piano / guitar
collocations.translation: 用钢琴/吉他为某人伴奏
collocations.example: A stranger stepped up to accompany the nervous singer on the guitar. （读后续写·舞台·善意）
She accompanied her warm words of welcome with a firm, reassuring handshake that instantly put the nervous newcomer at ease. （读后续写·迎新·细节）
The fierce wind was accompanied by driving rain that lashed the windows and blotted out the world beyond the glass. （读后续写·暴风雨·环境烘托）

collocations.phrase: a photograph / letter accompanying the report
collocations.translation: 随附报告的照片 / 信件
collocations.example: Please find the photographs accompanying this letter, which vividly capture the joyful moments of our charity event. （应用文·投稿信/汇报）
We must not overlook the hidden risks that accompany rapid technological change, however dazzling its benefits may appear. （议论文·科技双刃剑·警示句）
He accompanied his impassioned speech with sweeping gestures, and the audience found themselves swept along by his conviction. （议论文/读后续写·演讲·感染力）

synonyms.translation: 【课件·辨析】[U] 陪伴；陪同（keep sb company 陪伴某人）
synonyms.example: She stayed the night to keep her frightened little sister company. 她留下过夜陪伴受惊的妹妹。（课件·Integrated skills：company [U] 不可数，陪伴，动词短语 keep sb company = accompany sb）
synonyms.usage: 辨析：company 作"陪伴"讲时不可数[U]，用于 keep sb company（陪伴某人）=accompany sb；companion 是可数名词[C]，指"同伴、伙伴"具体的人。切勿混用

synonyms.translation: 【课件·辨析】[C] 同伴，伙伴（具体的人）
synonyms.example: For three long years the old dog was his only companion. 三年来，那条老狗是他唯一的伙伴。（课件·Integrated skills：companion [C] 可数，指同伴／伙伴，与 company[U] 区分）
synonyms.usage: 辨析：companion [C] 指"作伴的人/物"，可数、可复数(companions)；company [U] 指抽象的"陪伴"，不可数。记忆：keep sb company(陪伴) vs a travelling companion(旅伴)

synonyms.translation: 护送，陪同(以保护或引导)
synonyms.example: Two officers escorted the frightened witness through the jostling crowd of reporters. （读后续写·护送·紧张）
synonyms.usage: escort 强调出于保护、警戒或礼仪职责的陪同，常有正式或权威意味；accompany 更中性、更温情，泛指结伴同行

synonyms.example: A team of nurses attended the ailing professor day and night. （读后续写·病榻·关怀）
synonyms.usage: attend(作'陪伴/伴随'解)较正式、书面，常指侍从、护理或某现象伴生(如 attended by risks)；accompany 用法更广、更口语化，且可表'伴奏'

synonyms.example: 'Mind if I go with you?' he asked, already reaching for his coat. （读后续写·对话·随性）
synonyms.usage: go with 口语、随意，日常对话首选；accompany 更正式书面，用于应用文和高级叙事，且能表'伴奏、伴随发生'等 go with 无法表达的义项

advancedExpressions.expression: keep sb company (= accompany sb) 陪伴某人；company n.[U] 陪伴／companion n.[C] 同伴
advancedExpressions.example: A loyal companion (n.[C] 同伴) will always keep you company (n.[U] 陪伴) — that is, accompany you — through the darkest nights. （课件辨析：动词 accompany = keep sb company；company 不可数、companion 可数）

advancedExpressions.expression: accompany sb. to / be accompanied by / accompany sb. on the piano / accompanied by rain / risks that accompany sth.
advancedExpressions.example: Accompanied by her teacher, she was accompanied on the piano through a storm-lit night, undaunted by the risks that accompany any first performance. （一句串联"陪同/伴奏/伴随/随附风险"，覆盖 accompany 三大义）

advancedExpressions.expression: accompany → escort(护送) / attend(侍从·伴生) / go with(口语)
advancedExpressions.example: Two guards escorted the guest, a nurse attended the patient, a friend simply went with me — yet all three, in their way, accompanied someone in need. （escort 正式护卫、attend 侍从/护理、go with 口语随行，accompany 最通用且能表"伴奏"）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·过去分词作伴随/后置定语
advancedExpressions.expression: ..., accompanied by ..., ... / the noun accompanying ...
advancedExpressions.example: She walked in, accompanied by loud applause, while the letter accompanying the parcel explained everything. （accompanied by 作伴随状语；accompanying 作后置定语，区分主动/被动）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., accompanied by ..., ...
advancedExpressions.example: She stepped onto the frozen stage, accompanied by a wave of applause that washed over her like sudden warmth on a winter's day. （过去分词短语作伴随状语，一句同时交代动作与氛围，画面浓缩）

advancedExpressions.expression: It would be my honour to accompany ... and ...
advancedExpressions.example: It would be my honour to accompany the visiting delegation throughout their stay and to ensure that every moment of their trip is both comfortable and memorable. （It would be my honour正式表意愿 + and并列承诺，展现服务姿态）

advancedExpressions.expression: Every ... is inevitably accompanied by ...; the wise ... rather than ...
advancedExpressions.example: Every great opportunity is inevitably accompanied by an equal measure of risk; the wise embrace both with open eyes rather than chase reward while turning a blind eye to danger. （be accompanied by 构建"机遇伴随风险"的辩证论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: My friend went with me to the hospital and I felt better.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Though I had told no one of my fear, my friend quietly accompanied me to the hospital, and the mere warmth of her presence beside me loosened the knot of dread that had tightened in my chest all morning. （读后续写·陪伴·心理描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Though让步开头制造反差 + accompany替换went with提升正式度 + 具体心理意象(loosened the knot of dread)代替'felt better' + 时间细节(all morning)

sentenceUpgrade.original: New chances always have risks.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Every new chance we seize is inevitably accompanied by a shadow of risk; yet it is precisely by walking hand in hand with uncertainty that the courageous carve out extraordinary lives. （议论文·机遇与风险）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: be accompanied by被动伴随结构 + 隐喻(shadow of risk, walking hand in hand) + it is precisely by...that强调句 + 抽象名词化(uncertainty)

classPractice.question: 雷声常常伴随着闪电而来。（用 accompany）
classPractice.note: 【课件·Integrated 翻译】accompany 表"伴随/同时发生"；主语 Lightning 单数、陈述一般规律用一般现在时 accompanies

classPractice.question: 请陪我去故乡走一走。（用 accompany）
classPractice.answer: Please accompany me on the trip to my hometown.
classPractice.note: 【课件·Integrated 翻译】accompany sb (on the trip) to somewhere 陪同某人（去某地）

classPractice.question: 玛丽唱歌，我弹钢琴给她伴奏。（用 accompany）
classPractice.answer: Mary sang and I accompanied her on / at the piano.
classPractice.note: 【课件·Integrated 翻译】accompany sb on / at the piano 用钢琴为某人伴奏；叙述过去用过去式 accompanied

classPractice.question: I don't think it's necessary for parents to accompany their children ____ college.
classPractice.note: 【课件·Integrated 语法填空】accompany sb to somewhere 陪同某人去某地，介词用 to

classPractice.question: While she was singing on the stage, her mother was accompanying her ____ the piano.
classPractice.note: 【课件·Integrated 语法填空】accompany sb at / on the piano 用钢琴为某人伴奏，介词 at 或 on 皆可

classPractice.question: The school rules state that no child shall be allowed out of the school unless ____ (accompany) by an adult.
classPractice.note: 【课件·Integrated 语法填空】unless (they are) accompanied by an adult，被动语态用过去分词；be accompanied by 由……陪同

classPractice.question: Children must be ____ (accompany) by an adult when they enter the laboratory.
classPractice.note: be accompanied by 被……陪同；此处为被动语态，用过去分词 accompanied

classPractice.question: 真正的成长总是伴随着不适。Genuine growth is always ____ ____ discomfort.
classPractice.note: be accompanied by sth. 伴随着某事（表伴随发生），介词用 by

classPractice.question: The old teacher gently ____ (accompany) the trembling girl on the piano, and she was no longer alone.
classPractice.note: accompany sb. on the piano 为某人钢琴伴奏；叙述过去用过去式 accompanied

translation: 预期，预料；期望，盼望；期待，盼望
original_sentence: It has helped me look to the future with expectation and now it helps me reflect on my life with quiet satisfaction.
readingExamples: It has helped me look to the future with expectation and now it helps me reflect on my life with quiet satisfaction.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a belief that something will probably happen or be the case
(2) n. a strong hope or feeling of eager anticipation that something good will happen
(3) n. (usually plural) a standard of behaviour, achievement or quality that someone hopes or demands
(4) n. what is regarded as likely to happen, used in phrases about meeting or exceeding it

posExamples.sentence: On the eve of the results, I lay awake with a heart torn between hope and dread, my whole future seeming to hang on that single envelope, heavy with the expectation of years. （读后续写·放榜前夜·煎熬）
I am writing in the joyful expectation that our proposal for a school recycling programme will win your wholehearted support and be put into practice this term. （应用文·倡议信）
When we place unrealistic expectations upon the young, we risk crushing the very curiosity and courage that true education is meant to nurture. （议论文·教育与压力·观点句）
The little boy pressed his nose against the frosted window, his eyes shining with the pure expectation of a child who believes, without a shred of doubt, that snow means magic. （读后续写·儿童·纯真期待）

wordForms.noun: expectation / expectancy（预期，寿命等的预期值）
wordForms.adjective: expectant（期待的；怀孕的）/ expected（预期的）/ unexpected（意外的）
wordForms.other: 构词法：expect(动词) → expectation(名词后缀 -ation) → expectant(形容词后缀 -ant)。搭配辨析：expect 常接 sb. to do／that 从句，而名词 expectation 表‘期望’时常用复数 expectations，搭配 meet/exceed/live up to；固定短语 beyond expectation 用单数。

idioms.example: Against all expectations, the timid boy who had never spoken in class rose to deliver a speech so moving that the whole hall fell silent. （读后续写·逆袭·反转）

idioms.translation: 远超某人最大胆的期望
idioms.example: The turnout for our charity sale exceeded our wildest expectations, and by noon every stall stood proudly empty. （应用文·活动汇报·成果）
Terrified of failing to live up to his father's expectations, he trained until his hands blistered, refusing to let a single day slip by wasted. （读后续写·压力与努力·心理）

collocations.translation: 达到／超出某人的期望（考点核心短语，注意 expectations 常用复数）
collocations.example: Her final score not only met but far exceeded everyone's expectations. 她的最终成绩不仅达到、还远超了所有人的期望。
The turnout was good beyond all expectation. 到场人数好得出乎意料。
Contrary to expectations, the youngest player won. 出乎意料的是，最年轻的选手赢了。
It has helped me look to the future with expectation and now it helps me reflect on my life with quiet satisfaction. 它让我满怀期待地展望未来，如今又让我平静满足地回顾人生。（课文原句）
Determined to meet the expectations of the teacher who had believed in her, she poured every spare hour into perfecting her essay. （读后续写·回报信任·奋斗）
The final performance surpassed all our expectations, leaving even the sternest judges nodding in unguarded admiration. （读后续写·比赛·惊艳）
When the long-awaited trip fell far short of our expectations, we learned that reality rarely wears the golden colours of our dreams. （读后续写·失望·哲思）

collocations.phrase: have high / low expectations of sb.
collocations.translation: 对某人有很高 / 很低的期望
collocations.example: Because my coach had such high expectations of me, I dared not give anything less than my absolute best. （读后续写·教练·激励）
The whole village gathered by the river in expectation of the returning fishermen, straining their eyes toward the empty horizon. （读后续写·守望·环境）
A wise leader knows when to raise expectations to inspire and when to lower them to comfort. （议论文·领导力·辩证）
An air of breathless expectation filled the auditorium as the lights dimmed and the first violin lifted its bow. （读后续写·演出前·氛围）
Advances in medicine have dramatically raised the average life expectancy, yet the deeper question remains: are we living longer, or merely dying more slowly? （议论文·医学与生命·反问）
It is the quiet, relentless expectation she holds of herself, rather than any prize, that keeps her working long after the others have gone home. （议论文·内驱力·观点）

synonyms.translation: 期待，预期(常含喜悦或紧张)
synonyms.example: She unwrapped the letter with trembling anticipation, savouring the delicious suspense of the unknown. （读后续写·拆信·情绪）
synonyms.usage: anticipation 更强调情绪上的兴奋、期待或紧张，重‘感受’；expectation 更侧重理性上认为某事很可能发生，或他人施加的标准，重‘判断/要求’

synonyms.example: Even in the darkest hour, a faint hope flickered in his chest, refusing to be snuffed out. （读后续写·绝境·信念）
synonyms.usage: hope 是主观愿望，未必有充分依据，情感色彩温暖；expectation 通常基于一定证据或理由，更接近‘预料/理应如此’，也可指外界的要求(标准)

synonyms.example: The prospect of leaving home for the first time filled her with a strange mixture of terror and thrill. （读后续写·离家·矛盾心理）
synonyms.usage: prospect 多指对未来某种前景或可能性的展望，常与 of doing 连用，可褒可贬；expectation 更强调‘预料会发生’或‘所要求达到的标准’

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·期望的达成与落空
advancedExpressions.expression: meet / live up to / exceed / surpass expectations（达到／不负／超出期望） ↔ fall short of / fail to meet expectations（未达期望）；beyond expectation / contrary to expectations（出乎意料）
advancedExpressions.example: The results exceeded our expectations, though the rehearsal had fallen far short of them just a week before. 结果超出了我们的期望，尽管一周前的排练还远未达到期望。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·表达期待的情绪
advancedExpressions.expression: look forward to sth. with expectation / anticipation；in eager expectation of；full of expectation（用来替换单调的 hope for）
advancedExpressions.example: We waited in eager expectation of the results. 我们满怀期待地等待结果。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·同源词的介词搭配
advancedExpressions.expression: have high expectations of sb.（对某人有高期望，用 of）；in expectation of sth.（指望，期待）；beyond / contrary to expectation（介词固定，不加 the）
advancedExpressions.example: Parents' high expectations of their children can either inspire or crush them. 父母对孩子的高期望既可能激励也可能压垮他们。

advancedExpressions.expression: contrary to all expectation, sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: Contrary to all expectation, it was the quietest child in the room who stepped forward, and in that single act of courage the whole meaning of the day was transformed. （contrary to all expectation制造戏剧反转，续写高潮段常用）

advancedExpressions.expression: It is my sincere expectation that ..., and I look forward to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is my sincere expectation that this exchange programme will bridge two cultures, and I look forward with great anticipation to welcoming your students on our campus. （It is my sincere expectation that正式表期望 + look forward to呼应，书信结尾套路）

advancedExpressions.expression: when expectations outrun reality, ...; only by ... can we ...
advancedExpressions.example: When our expectations outrun reality, disappointment is the inevitable price; only by grounding our hopes in honest effort can we spare ourselves the bitterness of a dream deferred.

sentenceUpgrade.original: I hoped to pass the exam and felt nervous waiting for the result.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the day of reckoning drew near, I hovered between soaring expectation and gnawing fear, each ring of the phone sending a jolt through me, for on that single result my entire future seemed precariously balanced. （读后续写·等待结果·心理煎熬）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: hover between A and B矛盾心理框架 + 生动动词(soaring, gnawing, jolt) + 细节触发(each ring of the phone) + 隐喻(precariously balanced)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Parents should not expect too much from their children.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When parents burden their children with expectations too heavy to bear, they may unwittingly extinguish the very spark of curiosity that genuine growth depends upon. （议论文·教育反思）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: When引导条件状语 + burden...with具象化压力 + unwittingly副词点出无意之失 + extinguish the spark隐喻 + the very...that强调

classPractice.question: Her performance in the final round far ____ (exceed) everyone's expectations, and the whole hall rose in applause.
classPractice.note: 考 exceed expectations 固定搭配，句中 rose 表明为过去时

classPractice.question:
出乎所有人的意料，那个平时最安静的男孩赢得了比赛。(expectation)
____ ____ ____ ____, the quietest boy won the competition.
classPractice.answer: Contrary to all expectations / Contrary to everyone's expectations
classPractice.note: 考 contrary to expectations 表‘与预期相反’，句首介词短语作状语

classPractice.question: My coach always had high expectations ____ me, so I never dared to slack off.
classPractice.note: 考 have high expectations of sb. 的介词搭配，用 of 不用 for

translation: 非凡的，卓越的，出色的，引人注目的
original_sentence: 3 How does the article about Beethoven’s remarkable life inspire you during difficult times?
readingExamples: 3 How does the article about Beethoven’s remarkable life inspire you during difficult times?
definitionEn:
(1) adj. unusual or surprising in a way that causes people to take notice; extraordinary
(2) adj. deserving admiration or attention because of being impressive, excellent or exceptional
(3) adj. worthy of being commented on or remarked upon

posExamples.sentence: What struck me most was not her flawless technique but the remarkable calm in her eyes — the calm of someone who had already made peace with the possibility of losing. （读后续写·比赛·人物刻画）
I am writing to nominate Li Hua for the Star Student Award, for she has shown remarkable perseverance in leading our volunteer team through one obstacle after another. （应用文·推荐信）
History teaches us that remarkable achievements are seldom the fruit of talent alone; more often, they spring from a stubborn refusal to surrender in the face of repeated defeat. （议论文·成就与坚持·主题句）
In the space of a single summer the shy, stammering boy had undergone a remarkable transformation, and the classmates who returned in autumn scarcely recognised him. （读后续写·蜕变·今昔对比）

wordForms.noun: remark（评论，话语）/ remarkableness（非凡）
wordForms.other: 构词法：remark(动词/名词) + 后缀 -able → remarkable，字面‘值得评论的’，引申为‘非凡的、显著的’。同类构词：note→notable, notice→noticeable。易混：remarkable(非凡的) ≠ remarked(被议论的)；副词 remarkably 常修饰形容词，如 remarkably good。

collocations.example: Winning three golds at seventeen was a remarkable achievement. 十七岁拿下三枚金牌是非凡的成就。

collocations.translation: 贝多芬非凡的一生（课文原句）
collocations.example: How does the article about Beethoven's remarkable life inspire you during difficult times? 关于贝多芬非凡一生的文章在困境中如何激励你？（课文原句）

collocations.translation: 值得注意／令人惊叹的是……（形式主语句型）
collocations.example: It is remarkable that a deaf man could compose such music. 一个失聪的人竟能谱写出这样的音乐，实在令人惊叹。

collocations.translation: 非常地，惊人地（副词修饰）
collocations.example: She stayed remarkably calm during the crisis. 危机中她保持得异常镇定。
Under her patient guidance, the struggling class made remarkable progress, and by term's end even the weakest students walked with their heads held high. （读后续写·师恩·成长）
The old woman in the portrait bore a remarkable resemblance to my late grandmother, and I stood rooted before it, unable to look away. （读后续写·画像·情感触动）

collocations.translation: 非凡的勇气 / 毅力 / 决心
collocations.example: It was her remarkable perseverance, not any stroke of luck, that finally carried her across the finish line. （议论文·毅力·强调）

collocations.translation: 简直可谓非凡(强调语气)
collocations.example: The recovery of the injured athlete was nothing short of remarkable, defying every gloomy prediction the doctors had made. （读后续写·康复·奇迹）
The mentor changed my life in a remarkable way, teaching me not merely how to write, but how to see. （读后续写·恩师·升华）

collocations.translation: 在某方面有非凡的天赋
collocations.example: The child showed a remarkable talent for music, picking out melodies on the piano before she could even read. （读后续写·天赋·惊叹）

collocations.translation: 非常地好 / 平静 / 相似(副词)
collocations.example: Despite the chaos around her, she remained remarkably calm, issuing clear instructions that steadied everyone within earshot. （读后续写·危机·领导力）

synonyms.example: It took an extraordinary act of kindness from a total stranger to restore his faith in humanity. （读后续写·善意·主题）
synonyms.usage: extraordinary 强调超出寻常范围、非同一般，程度可正可负(如 extraordinary cruelty)；remarkable 侧重‘引人注目、值得称道’，几乎总是褒义或中性，语气略温和

synonyms.example: Her outstanding performance in the final round earned her a standing ovation. （读后续写·比赛·夺冠）
synonyms.usage: outstanding 强调在众人之中出类拔萃、成绩优异，多用于能力、表现、成就；remarkable 更强调‘令人惊讶、值得留意’，不一定是‘最好’，而是‘不寻常’

synonyms.example: Only students of exceptional ability are admitted to the programme. （议论文/应用文·选拔·标准）
synonyms.usage: exceptional 强调罕见地优秀或属于例外情况，语气正式、评价高；remarkable 更口语常用，侧重‘引起注意的不寻常’，褒贬程度略低于 exceptional

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·It is remarkable that + 陈述语气
advancedExpressions.expression: It is remarkable that + 主语 + 一般时（表‘令人惊叹／值得注意的是’，从句用陈述语气，不用虚拟）
advancedExpressions.example: It is remarkable that she learned to play the piano entirely on her own. 令人惊叹的是，她完全靠自学会了弹钢琴。

advancedExpressions.expression: nothing short of remarkable（简直非凡）；truly / genuinely remarkable（着实非凡）；a remarkable + 抽象名词（achievement / feat / talent / resemblance）
advancedExpressions.example: His comeback was nothing short of remarkable. 他的复出简直堪称非凡。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·夸赞出色（写作替换 good/great）
advancedExpressions.expression: remarkable / extraordinary / outstanding / exceptional（辨析见 synonyms）——用来替换平淡的 very good，提升语域
advancedExpressions.example: The team showed remarkable teamwork, outstanding discipline and exceptional courage. 团队展现了非凡的协作、出色的纪律与卓越的勇气。

advancedExpressions.expression: what was truly remarkable was not ... but ...
advancedExpressions.example: What was truly remarkable was not that she won, but that she smiled as warmly at the girl who beat her as she had at her own reflection in triumph. （what从句作主语强调 + not...but转折，突出人物精神境界，续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. deserves ... for the remarkable ... she has demonstrated
advancedExpressions.example: Li Hua richly deserves this honour for the remarkable dedication she has demonstrated, sacrificing weekend after weekend to tutor children in the mountain village. （deserve...for引出理由 + remarkable+抽象名词 + 分词短语补充事迹，推荐信有力）

advancedExpressions.expression: behind every remarkable ... lies ...
advancedExpressions.example: Behind every remarkable success lies a mountain of unseen effort — the sleepless nights, the silent tears, and the thousand small victories that no applause ever records.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She did very well and everyone was surprised.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Her performance was nothing short of remarkable, and a stunned silence gripped the hall before it erupted into a thunderous, disbelieving applause. （读后续写·惊艳全场·氛围）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: nothing short of remarkable强调结构 + before连接前后反应制造节奏 + 感官动词(gripped, erupted) + 递进形容词(thunderous, disbelieving)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Great success needs hard work, not just talent.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Behind every remarkable accomplishment lies not the effortless gift of talent, but the quiet, relentless toil that the applauding world never sees. （议论文·成功与努力）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Behind...lies倒装句式营造深度 + remarkable修饰核心名词 + not...but对比talent与toil + relentless/quiet形容词强化 + 定语从句(the world never sees)

translation: vi. & vt. 流动而行，涌动；流，流动 | n. 小溪；(人)流，(车)流
original_sentence: 5 10 15 20 On 7 May 1824, a crowd of music lovers streamed into a theatre in Vienna to hear the first-ever performance of the great Ludwig van Beethoven’s Symphony No.
readingExamples: 5 10 15 20 On 7 May 1824, a crowd of music lovers streamed into a theatre in Vienna to hear the first-ever performance of the great Ludwig van Beethoven’s Symphony No.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a small narrow river
(2) n. a continuous flow of liquid, gas, people, vehicles or things
(3) vi. to move or flow in a continuous flow, especially in large numbers or amounts
(4) vt./vi. to play or transmit video or audio data over the internet in a continuous flow rather than downloading it first

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】鱼贯而行，大量地移动/行进（to move somewhere in large numbers）
uncommonMeanings.example: People streamed across the bridge. 桥上行人川流不息。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】（连续地）流动，流出（to move or pour out in a continuous flow）
uncommonMeanings.example: Tears streamed down his face. 眼泪顺着他的脸往下流。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】流播，在线播放；按能力给学生分班
uncommonMeanings.example: You can stream the whole album on their website. 你可以在他们网站上在线播放整张专辑。He advocates streaming children according to their needs. 他主张按能力给孩子分班，因材施教。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 溪流，小河（本义）
uncommonMeanings.example: A clear mountain stream ran past the cottage. 一条清澈的山间小溪从小屋旁流过。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 一股，一串，川流不息的一片（人流／车流／液体等）
uncommonMeanings.example: A steady stream of visitors filed through the gate. 川流不息的游客鱼贯穿过大门。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 涌动，流动而行（大量地移动，如人群涌入；课文用法）
uncommonMeanings.example: Fans streamed into the stadium the moment the gates opened. 大门一开，球迷便涌入了体育场。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 在线播放，流媒体传输（现代高频义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Millions streamed the concert live that night. 那晚数百万人在线观看了这场音乐会直播。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (按能力分的)学生班组，能力分层组(英式教育)
uncommonMeanings.example: Placed in the top stream for mathematics, she felt for the first time that her quiet years of struggle had finally been noticed. （读后续写·分班·被看见的喜悦）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (按能力)给(学生)分班，分层教学
uncommonMeanings.example: The school's decision to stream pupils by ability sparked a heated debate among the parents at the meeting. （议论文·教育公平·争议话题）

posExamples.sentence: The moment the gates swung open, thousands of eager spectators streamed into the stadium, a restless river of colour and noise surging toward the stands. （读后续写·入场·人潮画面）
We followed the winding stream deep into the woods, its clear water chattering over the pebbles as if telling secrets to the trees. （读后续写·郊游·感官描写）
I would like to propose that a steady stream of student volunteers be organised throughout the exhibition, so that no visitor is ever left without a friendly guide. （应用文·建议信）
In an age when information streams at us from every screen, the rarest and most valuable skill may well be the ability to pause, filter and think for ourselves. （议论文·信息时代·观点句）

wordForms.noun: stream（溪流；一股）/ streamer（飘带；主播）/ streaming（流媒体，动名词转名词）
wordForms.adjective: streaming（流动的；流媒体的，如 a streaming service）
wordForms.other: 构词法：动名词 streaming 已固化为名词/形容词，指‘流媒体’（streaming platform 流媒体平台）。一词多用要点：stream 既是名词（溪流／一股）又是动词（涌动／在线播放），做题时先按句法判断词性，再定词义。易混：stream(溪流)＜river(河流)＜brook(诗意小溪)。

idioms.idiom: go against / swim against the stream
idioms.example: It takes rare courage to swim against the stream, to hold fast to your convictions when the whole crowd is rushing the other way. （议论文·独立思考·观点）
For years he had simply gone with the stream, doing what was expected, until one sleepless night he asked himself whether the life he led was truly his own. （读后续写·觉醒·心理转折）

idioms.translation: 意识流(思绪不断的流动)
idioms.example: Her diary read like a stream of consciousness, one thought tumbling into the next without pause or punctuation. （读后续写·内心独白·风格）

collocations.translation: 【课件】鱼贯而行，川流不息地移动（大量地涌动、行进）
collocations.example: People streamed across the bridge. 桥上行人川流不息。He stared out of the window at the cars streaming along the street. 他望着窗外沿街川流不息的车流。

collocations.translation: 【课件】（泪水、液体等）流动，流出，不断淌下
collocations.example: Tears streamed down his face. 眼泪顺着他的脸往下流。

collocations.phrase: an endless / constant / steady stream of sth.
collocations.translation: 【课件】络绎不绝的 / 接连不断的 / 源源不断的（人流、车流、询问、工作等）
collocations.example: Cars filed past in an endless stream. 汽车川流不息地驶过。a constant stream of enquiries 接连不断的询问；I've had a steady stream of visitors. 我这儿访客络绎不绝；a steady stream of work 接连不断的工作。
If you visit their website, you can stream the whole album. 如果你访问他们的网站，就可以在线播放整张专辑。

collocations.translation: 【课件】按能力给（学生）分班，分层教学
collocations.example: He advocates streaming children, and educating them according to their needs. 他主张按能力给孩子分班，并根据他们的需要因材施教。

collocations.translation: 涌入 / 涌出某处（课文用法）
collocations.example: On 7 May 1824, a crowd of music lovers streamed into a theatre in Vienna to hear Beethoven's Symphony No. 9. 1824年5月7日，一群乐迷涌入维也纳一家剧院聆听贝多芬第九交响曲。（课文原句·已清理提取碎片）

collocations.phrase: a stream of people / traffic / visitors
collocations.translation: 川流不息的人群 / 车流 / 游客
collocations.example: An endless stream of visitors filed past the ancient scroll. 络绎不绝的游客从古画卷前经过。

collocations.phrase: stream music / a film / a match
collocations.translation: 在线播放音乐／电影／比赛（流媒体）
collocations.example: Most teenagers now stream music instead of buying CDs. 如今大多数青少年在线听音乐，而不再买CD。

collocations.translation: 山间小溪 / 清澈的溪流
collocations.example: At the foot of the hill a clear stream wound its way through the meadow, sparkling wherever the sunlight touched it. （读后续写·风景·画面）
A steady stream of donations poured in after the appeal, and within a week the target had been comfortably met. （应用文·募捐汇报·成果）

collocations.phrase: tears / sweat stream down sb.'s face
collocations.translation: 泪水 / 汗水从脸上淌下
collocations.example: Tears streamed silently down her weathered cheeks as she watched her son's ship shrink into the grey horizon. （读后续写·送别·情感）

collocations.translation: 光线 / 阳光倾泻而入
collocations.example: Golden sunlight streamed through the dusty window, and for a moment the shabby little room seemed touched with magic. （读后续写·环境·希望氛围）

collocations.phrase: a stream of abuse / questions / ideas
collocations.translation: 连珠炮似的谩骂 / 问题 / 一连串想法
collocations.example: The reporters unleashed a stream of questions, but she answered each one with unshakable composure. （读后续写·采访·镇定）

collocations.translation: (工厂、设备等)投入运行；(资源)可用
collocations.example: Once the new solar plant comes on stream, the town's reliance on coal will fall dramatically. （议论文·能源转型·例证）

collocations.translation: 在线播放电影 / 音乐会 / 比赛
collocations.example: Unable to attend in person, thousands of alumni streamed the anniversary ceremony, united across continents by a single flickering screen. （议论文/应用文·数字联结·场景）

synonyms.example: Messages of support flooded in the moment the news broke, overwhelming her with unexpected warmth. （读后续写·关怀·情感）
synonyms.usage: flood 强调突然、大量、势不可挡地涌来，气势更猛、更满溢；stream 强调连续不断地‘流动’，更有方向感和持续性，未必是压倒性的量

synonyms.example: Crowds poured out of the theatre and spilled onto the rain-slick street. （读后续写·散场·人潮）
synonyms.usage: pour 强调大量而急促地倾泻或涌出，动作猛烈；stream 更平稳、更连绵，像溪水般持续流动，画面更细腻悠长

synonyms.example: A bubbling brook meandered through the sunlit glade. （读后续写·田园·文学描写）
synonyms.usage: brook 是较文学化、诗意的‘小溪’，多见于写景抒情；stream 更通用中性，既可指小溪，也可指人流、车流、气流乃至流媒体，义项远比 brook 丰富

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·‘一股／川流不息’的量化表达
advancedExpressions.expression: a stream of + n.（一股／一连串）；a steady stream of（源源不断的）；an endless stream of（络绎不绝的）——用来替换 many/a lot of，画面更动态
advancedExpressions.example: A steady stream of volunteers kept the relief effort going. 源源不断的志愿者让救援得以持续。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·大量涌动（辨析 flood / pour / stream）
advancedExpressions.expression: people streamed / poured / flooded into...（涌入）：stream 连绵有方向，pour 急促，flood 势不可挡——续写描人潮可分级选用
advancedExpressions.example: As the doors opened, spectators streamed in; then, when the star appeared, they positively flooded toward the stage. 门一开观众便涌入；明星一现身，他们更是潮水般拥向舞台。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·stream 的词性判断
advancedExpressions.expression: 名词：a stream of + 名词；动词：主语 + stream + into/out of/down（不及物）或 stream + 宾语（及物，如 stream music）
advancedExpressions.example: Crowds streamed out (v.) in a stream of colour (n.). 人群涌出，汇成一片色彩的洪流。

advancedExpressions.expression: sb./sth. streamed into ..., a river of ... surging ...
advancedExpressions.example: The moment the doors opened, spectators streamed into the arena, a living river of anticipation surging toward the brightly lit stage. （stream+同位语‘a river of...surging’双重比喻，把人群拍成动态画面，续写场面描写）

advancedExpressions.expression: I propose that a steady stream of ... be arranged so that ...

advancedExpressions.expression: in an age when ... streams at us ..., the real challenge is to ...
advancedExpressions.example: In an age when information streams at us from every direction, the real challenge is no longer to gather knowledge but to sift the trivial from the true.

translation: 热情的，热心的
original_sentence: The crowd immediately recognized that they were listening to something truly special, and they broke into enthusiastic cheers at the end of the symphony.
readingExamples: The crowd immediately recognized that they were listening to something truly special, and they broke into enthusiastic cheers at the end of the symphony.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. feeling or showing a lot of excitement and interest about something
(2) adj. eager to be involved in a particular activity that one enjoys
(3) adj. expressing strong approval or keen support for something

posExamples.sentence: No sooner had the final note faded than the audience leapt to their feet, breaking into such enthusiastic applause that the very rafters seemed to tremble with joy. （读后续写·演出·全场沸腾）
We are looking for enthusiastic volunteers who are willing to give up their weekends to bring a little warmth and laughter to the children at the orphanage. （应用文·招募通知）
An enthusiastic learner does not wait to be pushed; driven by curiosity itself, he seeks out knowledge the way a thirsty traveller seeks a spring. （议论文·学习热情·类比论证）
Though her voice shook at first, the boy's enthusiastic nods from the front row gave her the courage to press on, and soon the words flowed freely. （读后续写·鼓励·相互支撑）

wordForms.noun: enthusiasm（热情，热忱，n. 不可数）/ enthusiast（热衷者，爱好者）
wordForms.verb: enthuse（对……热情洋溢地说；使热情，较少用）
wordForms.adjective: enthusiastic（热情的）/ enthused（充满热情的）
wordForms.other: 构词法：enthusiasm(名词) + 后缀 -tic → enthusiastic(形容词) → enthusiastically(副词)。名词 enthusiasm 拼写易错，双写要点‘en-thu-si-asm’，为不可数名词，常搭配 with great enthusiasm / show enthusiasm for。词族记忆：enthusiasm(热情) - enthusiastic(热情的) - enthusiastically(热情地)。

collocations.translation: 【课件】热情的 → 热情地 → 热情（名词） → 爱好者（lover）
collocations.example: They broke into enthusiastic cheers. 他们爆发出热烈的欢呼。The crowd cheered enthusiastically, showing great enthusiasm; every music enthusiast in the hall rose to their feet. 人群热情地欢呼，展现出极大的热情；场内每一位音乐爱好者都起立喝彩。（课件词族：enthusiastic / enthusiastically / enthusiasm / enthusiast）

collocations.translation: 对某事满怀热情（考点核心搭配，介词用 about）
collocations.example: She is enthusiastic about learning Chinese calligraphy. 她对学习中国书法满怀热情。

collocations.translation: 爆发出热烈的欢呼／掌声（课文原句）
collocations.example: The crowd immediately recognized that they were listening to something truly special, and they broke into enthusiastic cheers at the end of the symphony. 观众立刻意识到他们听到的是真正非凡的作品，交响曲结束时爆发出热烈的欢呼。（课文原句）

collocations.translation: 热烈的回应／欢迎；热心的支持者
collocations.example: The plan met with an enthusiastic response from every member. 这项计划得到了每位成员的热烈响应。
My classmates were less than enthusiastic about the idea at first, but their doubts melted away once the first game began. （读后续写·从冷淡到投入·转变）
The more the coach praised his small improvements, the more enthusiastic the once-reluctant boy became about training. （读后续写·激励·正向循环）

collocations.translation: 极其 / 真心 / 非常热情
collocations.example: She was genuinely enthusiastic, not for the sake of the prize, but for the sheer joy of doing something she loved. （议论文·内在热情·辨析）
The young violinist finished to a wave of enthusiastic applause that rolled through the hall like a warm, unstoppable tide. （读后续写·舞台·反响）
As an enthusiastic supporter of environmental protection, I firmly believe our school should lead the way in going plastic-free. （应用文·倡议信·表态）

collocations.translation: 对这个想法 / 计划很热心
collocations.example: Everyone in the club was enthusiastic about the plan to organise a charity concert for the flood victims. （应用文·倡议/组织·氛围）
The proposal met with such an enthusiastic response that the committee approved it on the very same afternoon. （应用文·活动汇报·成效）

synonyms.example: He spoke so passionately about protecting the wetlands that even the most indifferent listeners found themselves moved. （议论文/读后续写·环保·感染力）
synonyms.usage: passionate 程度更深、更持久，指发自内心的强烈热爱与投入，常与信念、事业相连；enthusiastic 更侧重外显的兴奋、积极与热情，未必如 passionate 那样深沉执着

synonyms.example: The eager freshmen crowded around the noticeboard, impatient to sign up for every club at once. （读后续写·新生·急切）
synonyms.usage: eager 强调急切地想做某事、跃跃欲试，指向具体行动或结果；enthusiastic 强调对事物本身充满热情和兴趣，情绪更饱满、更外放

synonyms.translation: 热衷的，热心的(英式常用)
synonyms.example: She has always been keen on debating, never missing a single practice. （应用文/读后续写·兴趣·投入）
synonyms.usage: keen(on) 较口语、英式，指对某活动很有兴趣、很上心；enthusiastic 语气更强、更正式，情感表达更充沛，且可修饰掌声、回应等‘热烈’的场面

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·表达热情（by 词性成组记）
advancedExpressions.expression: be enthusiastic about（形容词短语）→ show great enthusiasm for（名词短语）→ respond enthusiastically to（副词短语）：同一意思三种词性表达，写作换用更显功力
advancedExpressions.example: Enthusiastic about the cause, she showed such enthusiasm that others enthusiastically joined in. 她对这项事业满怀热情，热情之高使得他人也热忱地加入进来。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·热爱与投入（辨析 passionate/eager/keen）
advancedExpressions.expression: enthusiastic / passionate / eager / keen（见 synonyms）：程度 passionate＞enthusiastic＞keen；eager 偏‘急切想做’
advancedExpressions.example: He is enthusiastic about music, passionate about justice, and eager to help. 他热爱音乐，对正义充满激情，并渴望助人。

advancedExpressions.expression: enthusiasm(n.) → enthusiastic(adj., 加 -tic) → enthusiastically(adv., 加 -ally)：同类如 sarcasm→sarcastic→sarcastically
advancedExpressions.example: Her enthusiasm was infectious, and the class worked enthusiastically all afternoon. 她的热情富有感染力，全班热情地忙了整个下午。

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had ... than ... broke into enthusiastic ...
advancedExpressions.example: No sooner had she struck the final chord than the entire hall broke into enthusiastic applause, and a stranger beside me wiped away a tear he did not bother to hide. （no sooner...than倒装制造瞬时冲击 + broke into enthusiastic applause高潮 + 细节旁人落泪烘托感染力）

advancedExpressions.expression: we warmly welcome anyone who is enthusiastic about ... to join us
advancedExpressions.example: We warmly welcome anyone who is enthusiastic about protecting our environment to join us this Saturday, for every willing pair of hands brings our green dream one step closer. （we warmly welcome...to join us招募套路 + enthusiastic about限定人选 + for引导号召，通知/倡议信有力）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is not talent but an enthusiastic heart that ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is not raw talent but an enthusiastic heart, forever curious and forever willing, that ultimately carries a person farthest along the road of learning.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The audience clapped happily after the show.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The instant the curtain fell, the audience rose as one and broke into such enthusiastic applause that the sound seemed to lift the very roof, a thunderous tribute no words could have expressed. （读后续写·谢幕·热烈反响）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: The instant时间状语制造即时感 + rose as one整齐动作 + broke into enthusiastic applause高级搭配 + 夸张(lift the very roof) + 同位语升华(a thunderous tribute)

sentenceUpgrade.original: Students who love learning study better.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Students who bring an enthusiastic, questioning spirit to their studies invariably outshine those who learn merely out of duty, for genuine passion turns the dull labour of study into a joyful pursuit. （议论文·学习热情）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 定语从句(who bring...spirit)刻画主体 + enthusiastic+questioning形容词叠加 + invariably outshine对比 + for引导原因 + 隐喻(turns labour into pursuit)

classPractice.question: All the members were highly ____ (enthusiasm) about the plan to hold a charity concert.
classPractice.note: 考名词 enthusiasm 变形容词 enthusiastic，be enthusiastic about

classPractice.question: The audience responded ____ (enthusiastic), clapping until their hands grew sore.
classPractice.note: 考副词 enthusiastically 修饰动词 responded

他对志愿服务满怀热情，从不错过任何一次活动。(enthusiastic)
He ____ ____ ____ volunteering and never misses a single event.
classPractice.note: 考 be enthusiastic about sth. 固定搭配，介词 about

translation: (pl. handkerchiefs or handkerchieves) 手帕，手绢
original_sentence: She took out a clean handkerchief and gently wiped the tears from the little girl’s cheeks.
readingExamples: She took out a clean handkerchief and gently wiped the tears from the little girl’s cheeks.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a small square piece of cloth or soft paper that you use for wiping your nose, eyes or face
(2) n. a decorative square of folded cloth worn in a jacket pocket or knotted around the neck
(3) n. (often as a cultural symbol) a piece of cloth that is waved, dropped or offered as a signal of farewell, distress or affection

posExamples.sentence: As the train pulled slowly out of the station, Grandma pressed a faded handkerchief to her eyes, waving until our carriage melted into the grey distance. （读后续写·离别场景）
I am writing to remind every participant that, apart from a water bottle, a clean handkerchief and a sun hat are essential for the day-long hiking trip we have organised. （应用文·通知）
In an age of disposable tissues, the humble cotton handkerchief may seem outdated, yet its return would spare our landfills from millions of tonnes of paper waste each year. （议论文·环保主题）
Trembling, she unfolded the silk handkerchief her mother had embroidered decades ago, and the faint scent of jasmine brought the past rushing back in a single, aching wave. （读后续写·回忆·物件传情）

wordForms.noun: handkerchief（复数 handkerchiefs / handkerchieves 均可）
wordForms.other: 拼写难点（高频考点）：hand + kerchief（源自 chief 一词），注意中间的 -kerchief- 有 c 无 c 易错，且 d 不发音。复数两种写法：handkerchiefs 或 handkerchieves。构词：kerchief(方巾/头巾) + hand- 前缀 → 手帕。近亲词：kerchief(头巾)、neckerchief(围巾)。

collocations.phrase: wipe one's eyes / nose / tears with a handkerchief
collocations.translation: 用手帕擦眼睛／鼻子／眼泪（课文场景）
collocations.example: She took out a clean handkerchief and gently wiped the tears from the little girl's cheeks. 她拿出一块干净的手帕，轻轻擦去小女孩脸上的泪水。（课文原句）
From the deck of the departing ship, dozens of emigrants waved their handkerchiefs, each white square a fragile thread still tying them to the homeland below. （读后续写·告别）

collocations.phrase: take out / offer sb. a handkerchief
collocations.translation: 拿出／递给某人一块手帕
collocations.example: Seeing her in tears, the kind conductor quietly offered her a handkerchief. 见她流泪，好心的乘务员默默递给她一块手帕。
The old gentleman always carried a crisp handkerchief, ready to offer it to any stranger in tears. （读后续写·人物刻画）
Tucked into his breast pocket, a silk handkerchief added a touch of quiet elegance to his worn but well-kept suit. （读后续写·外貌细节）
The embroidered handkerchief, passed down through four generations, was the only heirloom the family had managed to save from the fire. （读后续写·传家物）
She unfolded the handkerchief with great care, as though something precious and easily broken lay hidden within its worn creases. （读后续写·悬念）
By the end of the farewell letter, her handkerchief was soaked with tears, yet her handwriting remained steady and full of hope. （读后续写·情感高潮）
A neatly folded pocket handkerchief peeked from his jacket, the final touch that transformed an ordinary outfit into a picture of refinement. （应用文·礼仪介绍）

collocations.phrase: wipe one's eyes / nose with a handkerchief
collocations.example: He wiped his eyes with a crumpled handkerchief, ashamed that a grown man could be so moved by a child's simple kindness. （读后续写·心理描写）
Seeing her struggle to hold back tears, the kind conductor quietly offered her a handkerchief and a reassuring nod. （读后续写·善意）

collocations.phrase: tie a knot in a handkerchief
collocations.translation: 在手帕上打个结(以备忘)
collocations.example: As a boy he would tie a knot in his handkerchief so as not to forget his mother's small errands, a habit that lingered long into adulthood. （读后续写·习惯溯源）

synonyms.example: She reached for a tissue rather than a cloth handkerchief, dabbing her nose before the interview began. （应用文·日常场景）
synonyms.usage: 指一次性纸巾,用完即丢;handkerchief 多为可重复使用的布料,更显传统或正式

synonyms.example: The farmer's wife wore a bright kerchief over her hair to keep the dust away as she worked in the fields. （读后续写·乡村场景）
synonyms.usage: 泛指方形布巾,常戴在头上或围颈;handkerchief 专指擦拭用的小方巾,尺寸更小

synonyms.example: He wiped his lips with a linen napkin before rising to propose a toast. （应用文·宴会礼仪）
synonyms.usage: 指餐桌上擦嘴的餐巾,用于就餐语境;与随身携带的 handkerchief 用途完全不同

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·手帕的动作搭配（续写高频细节）
advancedExpressions.expression: take out / pull out a handkerchief；wipe one's eyes/tears with a handkerchief；wave a handkerchief（告别）；press a handkerchief to one's eyes（拭泪）
advancedExpressions.example: She pressed a handkerchief to her eyes and waved until the train vanished. 她把手帕按在眼角，一直挥手到火车消失。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·擦拭／揩物（区分 handkerchief/tissue/napkin）
advancedExpressions.expression: handkerchief(可反复用的布手帕) vs. tissue(一次性纸巾) vs. napkin(餐巾)——见 synonyms，写作按场景精准选词
advancedExpressions.example: He offered her not a paper tissue but his own cotton handkerchief. 他递给她的不是纸巾，而是自己的棉布手帕。

advancedExpressions.expression: hand- 构成大量复合词：handkerchief(手帕)、handwriting(笔迹)、handshake(握手)、handful(一把)——记 handkerchief 时联想 hand 家族
advancedExpressions.example: With a handshake and a handkerchief pressed into her palm, he said goodbye. 他与她握手，并把一块手帕塞进她手心，道了别。

advancedExpressions.expression: a single handkerchief, waving / pressed ..., became the last thread that ...
advancedExpressions.example: A single white handkerchief, fluttering above the crowd, became the last fragile thread that bound the departing soldier to the family he might never see again. （以小物件承载离别情感,续写高潮段）

advancedExpressions.expression: do remember to bring ..., for ...
advancedExpressions.example: Do remember to bring a handkerchief and comfortable shoes, for the outdoor ceremony may last well into the warm afternoon. （通知类结尾贴心叮嘱,拉近与读者距离）

advancedExpressions.expression: even the humble ... reminds us that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Even the humble handkerchief reminds us that sustainable living is often less about grand gestures than about the small, reusable choices we make each day.

sentenceUpgrade.original: She cried and used her handkerchief.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Tears blurred her vision as she pressed the worn handkerchief to her cheek — its faded flowers, once so bright, seemed to weep along with her in the fading light of the platform. （读后续写·环境+心理交融）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: as 引导伴随动作 + 破折号补充细节 + 拟人(seemed to weep) + 环境烘托(fading light)

sentenceUpgrade.original: People used to carry handkerchiefs, but now they use tissues.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Where earlier generations once carried a cloth handkerchief as a matter of course, today's disposable tissues have quietly taken its place — a small shift that mirrors our broader drift towards a throwaway culture. （议论文·今昔对比）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Where 引导让步/对比状语从句 + as a matter of course 习语 + 破折号引出评论 + mirror 隐喻升华主旨

classPractice.question: She took out two clean ____ (handkerchief) from her bag and handed one to the crying child.
classPractice.note: 考复数拼写，two 提示复数，两种写法均可

classPractice.question: 她拿出一块干净的手帕，轻轻擦去孩子脸上的泪水。(handkerchief, wipe)
classPractice.answer: She took out a clean handkerchief and gently wiped the tears from the child's face. / She took out a clean handkerchief and gently wiped the tears off the child's face.
classPractice.note: 考 handkerchief 拼写与 wipe the tears from/off 搭配，仿课文原句

classPractice.question: 从 handkerchief / napkin 中选：At the dinner table, he wiped his lips with a linen ____.
classPractice.note: 辨析：餐桌擦嘴用 napkin(餐巾)；handkerchief 是随身擦拭的小手帕

translation: 巨大的，广阔的，大量的
original_sentence: From the mountaintop, we looked out over a vast plain that stretched as far as the eye could see.
readingExamples: From the mountaintop, we looked out over a vast plain that stretched as far as the eye could see.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. extremely large in size, area or extent
(2) adj. very great in degree or amount, especially when describing a difference, majority or scale
(3) adj. (of space, land or the sky) seemingly endless; so wide that it cannot easily be measured

posExamples.sentence: Standing at the cliff's edge, the boy gazed at the vast ocean stretching endlessly before him, and for the first time his troubles felt wonderfully small. （读后续写·壮阔景色·心境转变）
I am writing to invite you to our science exhibition, where a vast collection of student inventions will be on display throughout the whole of next week. （应用文·邀请信）
The vast majority of researchers now agree that reducing carbon emissions is not merely an option but an urgent necessity for the survival of future generations. （议论文·环保论证）
As the desert opened before them, a vast expanse of golden dunes rolled away to the horizon, silent and unbroken, dwarfing the tiny caravan crawling across it. （读后续写·环境描写·渺小感）

wordForms.noun: vastness（广阔，浩瀚）
wordForms.other: 构词法：vast(形容词) + 名词后缀 -ness → vastness；+ 副词后缀 -ly → vastly。搭配辨析：a vast majority of + 复数可数（绝大多数），a vast amount/quantity of + 不可数（大量）；副词 vastly 常修饰 different/improved/superior 等表‘差异／改善’的词。

collocations.translation: 绝大多数（考点固定搭配，谓语随 of 后名词单复数）
collocations.example: The vast majority of students supported the new plan. 绝大多数学生支持这项新计划。

collocations.phrase: a vast area / plain / expanse of
collocations.translation: 一大片辽阔的区域／平原（课文原句）
collocations.example: From the mountaintop, we looked out over a vast plain that stretched as far as the eye could see. 从山顶望去，我们眺望着一望无际的辽阔平原。（课文原句）

collocations.translation: 大量的（后接不可数名词）
collocations.example: The project required a vast amount of research. 这个项目需要大量的研究。

collocations.translation: 极大地，大大地（副词，程度极强）
collocations.example: The two plans are vastly different. 这两个方案有着天壤之别。
Below the aircraft lay a vast expanse of emerald rainforest, so dense and unbroken that it seemed untouched by human hands. （读后续写·俯瞰景色）
There is a vast difference between reading about kindness and actually practising it when no one is watching. （议论文·品德论证）

collocations.translation: 渊博的知识/丰富的经验
collocations.example: Drawing on his vast experience as a mountaineer, the old guide led the frightened tourists safely down the icy slope. （读后续写·危机化解）
The government launched a tree-planting campaign on a vast scale, transforming barren hills into rolling seas of green within a decade. （议论文·治理成效）
Compared with her hesitant first draft, this essay shows a vast improvement in both structure and vocabulary. （应用文·点评/反馈）
Gazing up at the vast reaches of the night sky, the young astronomer felt both humbled and strangely at home. （读后续写·仰望星空）
The cultural festival offered a vast array of activities, from calligraphy workshops to traditional dance performances. （应用文·活动介绍）
Educators increasingly recognise the vast potential of artificial intelligence to personalise learning for every single student. （议论文·科技教育）
A vast majority of the students voted in favour of extending the library's opening hours during the examination period. （应用文·调查报告）

synonyms.example: They live in a huge house on the edge of town. 他们住在城边一栋巨大的房子里。
synonyms.usage: huge 最口语、最通用，单纯强调‘大’，可修饰具体物或抽象量；vast 更书面，尤指空间／面积的辽阔无边（vast plain/ocean）或抽象的极大差异／数量（vast majority），画面上有‘一望无际’之感。句法上二者都作定语／表语，但 vast 极少修饰单个小物体。

synonyms.example: The immense pressure of the final match seemed to weigh on every player, yet their captain's calm smile eased the tension. （读后续写·比赛压力）
synonyms.usage: 强调分量、程度或影响之大,常用于抽象事物(压力、努力、价值);vast 更偏重空间与数量的辽阔

synonyms.example: The charity concert raised an enormous sum of money for children in remote mountain areas. （应用文·公益报道）
synonyms.usage: 口语和书面都常见,强调超出寻常的大;与 vast 常可互换,但 enormous 更中性通用,vast 更具画面上的辽阔感

synonyms.example: Her boundless enthusiasm for volunteering inspired the entire class to sign up for the community project. （读后续写·感染力）
synonyms.usage: 强调没有边界、没有尽头,多用于抽象的热情、能量、希望;vast 可修饰具体空间,boundless 偏抽象且更文学化

synonyms.example: After extensive preparation, the debate team walked onto the stage with quiet confidence. （议论文/应用文·准备充分）
synonyms.usage: 强调覆盖面广、涉及范围大(研究、准备、损失);vast 强调整体规模惊人,extensive 强调铺展得广

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·量大／面广的高级替换
advancedExpressions.expression: the vast majority of（绝大多数，替 most）；a vast amount of（大量，替 much）；a vast array of（各式各样，替 many kinds of）；on a vast scale（大规模地）
advancedExpressions.example: A vast array of measures, adopted on a vast scale, benefited the vast majority of residents. 大规模采取的各式举措惠及了绝大多数居民。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·‘大’的分级（辨析 vast/huge/immense/enormous）
advancedExpressions.expression: huge(口语通用) → enormous(超乎寻常) → immense(分量/影响) → vast(空间辽阔/绝大多数) → boundless(无边抽象)：见 synonyms
advancedExpressions.example: Beneath the vast, boundless sky lay a huge desert of immense silence. 在辽阔无垠的天空下，是一片巨大而无比寂静的沙漠。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·majority 的主谓一致
advancedExpressions.expression: the vast majority of + 复数名词 + 复数谓语（The vast majority of students are...）；the majority 单独作主语视为整体多用单数
advancedExpressions.example: The vast majority of the votes were in favour. 绝大多数选票都表示赞成。

advancedExpressions.expression: against the vast ..., sb / sth seemed ...
advancedExpressions.example: Against the vast, star-strewn sky, their little campfire seemed no more than a trembling spark, yet its warmth held the darkness at bay. （以辽阔反衬渺小,续写环境描写）

advancedExpressions.expression: a vast majority of ... reported / preferred ...
advancedExpressions.example: According to our survey, a vast majority of respondents preferred outdoor activities to indoor ones, which strongly supports our proposal. （用数据措辞增强说服力）

advancedExpressions.expression: the vast ... far outweighs the ...
advancedExpressions.example: The vast benefits of lifelong reading far outweigh the modest time it demands — a bargain few investments in life can ever match.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The sea was very big and made me feel small.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Before me stretched a vast, restless sea, its horizon dissolving into the pale sky, and beneath its immensity I felt myself shrink into a single, insignificant grain of sand. （读后续写·壮景+渺小感）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Before me stretched 倒装开头 + 现在分词 dissolving 描景 + beneath its immensity 状语 + 比喻(grain of sand)收束情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: Most people agree that education is important.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The vast majority of thoughtful observers now concur that education is not a privilege reserved for the few, but the single most powerful lever for lifting an entire society. （议论文·观点强化）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: The vast majority of 正式主语 + concur 高级动词替换 agree + not ... but 对比结构 + lever 隐喻突出教育的杠杆作用

classPractice.question: The ____ (vast) majority of the students in our school take part in at least one club activity.
classPractice.note: 考固定搭配 the vast majority of，此处填形容词原级 vast

classPractice.question: The two designs may look alike, but in quality they are ____ (vast) different.

translation: 有才华的，有天赋的
original_sentence: As a gifted child, Beethoven was pushed by his father to study music day and night.
readingExamples: As a gifted child, Beethoven was pushed by his father to study music day and night.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. having a natural ability to do something extremely well; talented
(2) adj. (of a child) exceptionally intelligent or having outstanding potential
(3) adj. having a lot of intelligence, skill or a particular quality in high measure

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 有天赋的，有才华的（本义，形容人）
uncommonMeanings.example: As a gifted child, Beethoven was pushed by his father to study music day and night. 作为一个有天赋的孩子，贝多芬被父亲逼着日夜学习音乐。（课文原句）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （作为礼物）被赠予的（gift 作动词的过去分词）
uncommonMeanings.example: The old violin, gifted to her by a teacher she had long since lost touch with, was the one possession she vowed never to sell. （读后续写·珍贵馈赠·睹物思人）

posExamples.sentence: As a gifted child, Beethoven was pushed relentlessly by his father to practise from dawn till dusk, yet within those long, lonely hours a rare genius was quietly taking shape. （读后续写·天才养成）
I am writing to recommend Li Hua, a remarkably gifted young pianist whose dedication and humility make her an ideal candidate for your summer music scholarship. （应用文·推荐信）
Society often celebrates the gifted, yet true excellence, as countless stories remind us, springs far more from disciplined effort than from raw talent alone. （议论文·天赋与努力）
The moment the shy newcomer picked up the chalk and solved the problem three ways, the whole class fell silent, sensing they were in the presence of a truly gifted mind. （读后续写·才华初现）

wordForms.noun: gift（天赋，礼物）/ giftedness（天资）
wordForms.verb: gift（赠予；gift sb. sth. / gift sth. to sb.）
wordForms.other: gift-wrapped (adj. 用礼品纸包装的)。构词法：gift(名词‘天赋／礼物’) + 后缀 -ed → gifted，兼表‘天生具有的’与‘被赠予的’双义，需按语境判断。搭配辨析：a gifted child(天才儿童) 用形容词义；be gifted at/in sth.(在某方面有天赋) 用形容词义；be gifted sth./gifted to sb.(被赠予) 用动词过去分词义。

collocations.translation: 有天赋的孩子／学生／音乐家（课文用法）
collocations.example: As a gifted child, Beethoven began to compose before the age of twelve. 作为天才儿童，贝多芬十二岁前就开始作曲。

collocations.translation: 在某方面有天赋（考点搭配：at + 具体技能，in + 领域）
collocations.example: She is gifted at painting and gifted in languages. 她在绘画上有天赋，在语言方面也颇具才华。

collocations.translation: 天生具有（某种才能／品质）
collocations.example: Gifted with an extraordinary memory, he could recite entire chapters after a single reading. （读后续写·人物特长）

collocations.translation: 极有天赋的/天生有才的
collocations.example: Though exceptionally gifted, she never once looked down on classmates who struggled to keep pace. （读后续写·谦逊品格）

collocations.translation: 在学业上/音乐上有天赋的
collocations.example: Academically gifted yet socially anxious, the boy found in the debate club the confidence he had long lacked. （读后续写·成长转变）
A gifted teacher does not merely pour knowledge into students but kindles in them a lasting hunger to learn. （议论文·教育本质）
The school launched a gifted and talented programme to ensure that bright minds were challenged rather than left to coast. （应用文·校园通知）
The programme was designed to nurture gifted students without ever letting them forget the value of hard work. （应用文·项目介绍）

collocations.translation: 天生具有（某种才能/品质）
collocations.example: Gifted with an extraordinary memory, he could recite entire chapters after a single reading. （读后续写·人物特长）

collocations.translation: 天才音乐家/艺术家/运动员
collocations.example: Even the most gifted athlete, our coach reminded us, is nothing without discipline and heart. （议论文·体育精神）

synonyms.example: The talented young dancer earned a standing ovation the very first time she stepped onto the professional stage. （读后续写·首秀成功）
synonyms.usage: 与 gifted 近乎同义，均指天赋出众；talented 用途最广、语气中性，gifted 更强调与生俱来、程度更高，常用于资优儿童

synonyms.example: Her brilliant solution to the century-old puzzle left even the professors speechless. （议论文/读后续写·智力）
synonyms.usage: 侧重智力或思维的耀眼、极其聪明；gifted 强调天赋潜能，brilliant 强调已展现的卓越表现

synonyms.example: The child displayed a prodigious talent for languages, mastering three by the age of ten. （读后续写·神童）
synonyms.usage: 语气最强、偏书面，形容才能大到令人惊叹；gifted 更常用、更平实，prodigious 多修饰 talent/ability 等抽象名词

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·‘有天赋’的搭配套装
advancedExpressions.expression: be gifted at (doing) sth.（擅长具体技能）；be gifted in + 领域；be gifted with + 天赋／品质；a gifted + 名词（child/musician/mind）
advancedExpressions.example: Gifted with perfect pitch and gifted at improvising, the boy was clearly gifted in music. 天生拥有绝对音感、又擅长即兴，这男孩显然在音乐上极有天赋。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·夸赞才华（辨析 gifted/talented/brilliant/prodigious）
advancedExpressions.expression: gifted / talented / brilliant / prodigious（见 synonyms）：gifted 强调与生俱来的潜能，talented 通用，brilliant 强调已展现的耀眼，prodigious 惊人
advancedExpressions.example: The gifted, talented, brilliant young pianist showed a prodigious range at just fourteen. 这位天赋异禀、才华横溢、光彩夺目的少年钢琴家，年仅十四便展现出惊人的表现力。

advancedExpressions.expression: gift(n.) 既指‘礼物’又指‘天赋’；派生 gifted 也据此分两义——‘有天赋的’(a gifted child) 与‘被赠予的’(the watch gifted to me)
advancedExpressions.example: Music was both a gift he was born with and a gift his father gave him. 音乐既是他与生俱来的天赋，也是父亲送给他的礼物。

advancedExpressions.expression: gifted though sb. was, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Gifted though he was, the young violinist knew that talent unaccompanied by practice was a candle that would soon burn out. （让步倒装开篇，欲扬先抑刻画谦逊主角）

advancedExpressions.expression: few students I have taught are as gifted as ...
advancedExpressions.example: In my twenty years of teaching, few students have been as gifted, and none as diligent, as the young woman I am recommending. （推荐信最高级评价，可信度高）

advancedExpressions.expression: being gifted is a starting point, not a guarantee of ...
advancedExpressions.example: Being gifted is merely a starting point, not a guarantee of success; the seed of talent withers unless watered by persistent effort. （辩证立论+比喻，纠正天赋决定论）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He was a gifted boy who loved music.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: There was something extraordinary about the boy the moment he lifted the bow — a gifted intensity in his eyes that hushed the room and made even the sceptics lean forward in their seats. （读后续写·才华具象化）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: There be 句型引出焦点 + the moment 时间从句抓瞬间 + 破折号补充细节 + 具体反应(hushed, lean forward)侧面烘托天赋

sentenceUpgrade.original: Gifted people still need to work hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: History offers no shortage of cautionary tales in which dazzlingly gifted individuals faded into obscurity, undone not by any lack of talent but by their refusal to cultivate it. （议论文·历史例证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: History offers no shortage of... 归纳式开篇 + in which 定语从句嵌入例证 + not by...but by 精准归因，强调努力

classPractice.note: 考 gift 的形容词 gifted，be gifted 表‘有天赋的’

她在数学上很有天赋，很小就能解出复杂的题目。(gifted, at)
She ____ ____ ____ maths and could solve complex problems at a very young age.
classPractice.note: 考 be gifted at (doing) sth. 表‘在某方面有天赋’，介词 at 接具体技能

classPractice.question: 从 gifted / talented 中选更强调‘与生俱来’的：The school runs a special programme for academically ____ children.
classPractice.note: 辨析：形容资优／天赋异禀的儿童常用 gifted（gifted children/programme），强调天生潜能

translation: 名誉，名声
original_sentence: By the time he was a teenager, he had already enjoyed a reputation as a wonderful young musician.
readingExamples: By the time he was a teenager, he had already enjoyed a reputation as a wonderful young musician.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the opinion that people in general have about someone or something, based on past behaviour or character
(2) n. the good name or public esteem that a person, institution or place has earned
(3) n. a widespread belief that someone or something has a particular characteristic

posExamples.sentence: By the time he was a teenager, Beethoven had already earned a reputation as a wonderful young musician, and audiences would fall silent the instant his fingers touched the keys. （读后续写·天才成名）
I am writing to assure you that our restaurant takes its reputation for hygiene extremely seriously, and we have already investigated the concern you raised. （应用文·回复信）
A good reputation, once shattered, is seldom fully restored; it is far easier to preserve integrity than to rebuild trust after it has been lost. （议论文·诚信论证）
For years the old craftsman had guarded his reputation like a fragile heirloom, and now, with one hasty forgery, an apprentice threatened to smash it beyond repair. （读后续写·危机时刻）

wordForms.noun: reputation（名声，名誉）/ repute（名望，书面）
wordForms.verb: repute（认为，据说；极少用，常见被动 be reputed to be/do）
wordForms.adjective: reputable（声誉好的，可信赖的）/ reputed（号称的，据说的）
wordForms.other: 构词法：repute(词根，与 compute/dispute 同根 -pute‘想，算’) + -ation → reputation。同族记忆：reputable(有好名声的，褒义) ↔ disreputable(名声差的)。易混：reputable(声誉好的) 与 reputed(据说的，如 the reputed author 据称的作者) 意义不同，勿混。

idioms.example: The little seaside inn more than lived up to its reputation, greeting us with warm bread, warmer smiles, and a view that stole our breath. （读后续写·旅途惊喜）

idioms.idiom: have a reputation to protect / uphold
idioms.example: As head prefect, she had a reputation to uphold, and so she reported the cheating even though the culprit was her closest friend. （读后续写·道德抉择）

collocations.phrase: enjoy a reputation as / for sth.
collocations.translation: 【课件】享有……的声誉（as 接身份 / for 接内容或原因）
collocations.example: By the time he was a teenager, he had already enjoyed a reputation as a wonderful young musician. 十多岁的时候，他已经是有名的杰出少年音乐家了。The company enjoys an international reputation for quality of design. 这家公司因设计质量而享有国际声誉。
The restaurant has a good reputation, and I heard nothing but praise about it. 这家餐厅名声很好，我听到的全是赞誉。
Through years of honest work, she earned a reputation that money could never buy. 靠着多年的诚实工作，她赢得了金钱无法买到的声誉。
He really lives up to his reputation as a "walking dictionary". 他真是名副其实的"活字典"。

collocations.translation: 【课件】损害 / 毁坏某人的名声
collocations.example: One careless lie can ruin a reputation built over decades. 一个不慎的谎言就能毁掉数十年建立起来的名声。

collocations.phrase: have a reputation for (doing) sth. / as sth.
collocations.translation: 以……著称，有……的名声（考点核心：for 接内容，as 接身份）
collocations.example: The restaurant has a reputation for excellent service. 这家餐厅以优质服务著称。
A good reputation is hard to earn but easy to lose. 好名声难得而易失。
By the time he was a teenager, he had already enjoyed a reputation as a wonderful young musician. 在他还是少年时，就已经享有了出色青年音乐家的声誉。（课文原句）
Through years of honest dealing, the small firm had built a reputation that money simply could not buy. （议论文·商业诚信）
A single dishonest headline can tarnish a newspaper's reputation for decades to come. （议论文·媒体责任）
Determined to restore his tarnished reputation, the young reporter spent a year chasing the truth others had buried. （读后续写·自我救赎）

collocations.phrase: at the risk of one's reputation
collocations.example: At the risk of his own reputation, the scientist published findings that overturned the very theory he had once championed. （议论文·科学良知）
It was her unshakeable reputation for honesty that made the whole village trust her account of that night. （读后续写·关键证词）
The professor had a reputation for pushing his students hard, yet every one of them left his class thinking bigger. （读后续写·严师）
The academy enjoys an international reputation for turning shy beginners into confident performers. （应用文·机构介绍）

synonyms.example: Overnight fame swept the young singer off her feet, but it was her humility that kept her grounded. （读后续写·成名代价）
synonyms.usage: 侧重广为人知的知名度、名气大小，可中性或褒义；reputation 侧重公众对其品格/能力的评价（可好可坏）

synonyms.translation: 威望，声誉（尤指令人尊敬的地位）
synonyms.example: Winning the national award lent the school an air of prestige it had never enjoyed before. （应用文·校园荣誉）
synonyms.usage: 强调因成就或地位而赢得的尊崇与影响力，褒义；reputation 更中性宽泛，prestige 层次更高、更正式

synonyms.example: A scholar of great renown, she was invited to lecture at universities across three continents. （议论文/应用文·学术）
synonyms.usage: 书面、偏正式，指因卓越成就而广受尊敬的盛名，褒义色彩强；日常评价用 reputation，颂扬名家用 renown

synonyms.example: The scandal severely weakened his standing within the community. （议论文·社会评价）
synonyms.usage: 侧重在某群体中的地位与受尊重程度，常与 social/professional 连用；reputation 更强调外界对其的普遍看法

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·who 引导非限制性定语从句（课件语法点）
advancedExpressions.expression: who 引导非限制性定语从句，对先行词（人）作补充说明，用逗号与主句隔开，不可用 that 替换：先行词, who + 谓语, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Beethoven, who was almost completely deaf at this point in his life, was unaware of the audience's response until one of the singers turned him around to face the crowd. 当时贝多芬已近全聋，直到一位领唱扶他转过身来面向观众，他才发觉反响之热烈。（课件原句·who 非限制性定语从句 + not...until 时间状语从句同现）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·until 引导时间状语从句（not...until 直到才）（课件语法点）
advancedExpressions.expression: not + 主句谓语 + until + 从句：直到……才……；主句谓语须用非延续性动词或用否定式，until 引导时间状语从句
advancedExpressions.example: The Smiths, who were having lunch, didn't know the arrival of a package until a knock on the door asked them to open it. 史密斯夫妇当时正在吃午饭，听到有人敲门、打开门才知道快递到了。（课件仿写答案·who 非限制性定语从句 + not...until 时间状语从句）

advancedExpressions.expression: build / earn / establish a reputation（树立名声） ↔ damage / ruin / tarnish / destroy a reputation（毁名声）；live up to one's reputation（名副其实）；have a reputation for（以……著称）
advancedExpressions.example: It took decades to build the reputation that one scandal nearly ruined overnight. 这份用数十年树立的名声，一场丑闻几乎一夜毁掉。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·名声／声望（辨析 fame/prestige/renown/standing）
advancedExpressions.expression: reputation(评价，可褒可贬) / fame(名气) / prestige(威望，褒) / renown(盛名，书面) / standing(地位)：见 synonyms
advancedExpressions.example: Her reputation for integrity, more than her fame or prestige, secured her lasting standing in the field. 使她在业内地位长存的，是她正直的名声，而非名气或威望。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·reputation 的介词搭配
advancedExpressions.expression: a reputation for + 名词/doing（因……而闻名）；a reputation as + 身份（作为……的名声）；at the risk of one's reputation（冒名声之险）
advancedExpressions.example: He earned a reputation as a fair judge and a reputation for never taking a bribe. 他赢得了公正法官的名声，也有着从不受贿的声誉。

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. would rather ... than stain a reputation built over ...
advancedExpressions.example: He would rather lose the contract than stain a reputation built over thirty years of honest craftsmanship. （would rather...than 抉择句式，突出人物操守）

advancedExpressions.expression: with a well-deserved reputation for ..., we are proud to ...
advancedExpressions.example: With a well-deserved reputation for nurturing young talent, our club is proud to open its doors to every eager beginner this term. （招募/宣传信开篇，以声誉背书增强吸引力）

advancedExpressions.expression: a reputation takes years to build but only moments to destroy
advancedExpressions.example: A reputation takes years to build but only moments to destroy — a truth that ought to make us weigh every word before we speak in the age of social media. （警句式对比，点明诚信在网络时代的分量）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He was famous as a good young musician.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Before he had even outgrown his boyhood, his name travelled from parlour to concert hall, until a reputation as the most gifted young musician of his generation preceded him wherever he went. （读后续写·声名远扬）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Before 时间从句制造成长弧线 + travelled 拟人化传播 + until 从句层层推进 + preceded him 生动表现名声在先

sentenceUpgrade.original: It is hard to get your reputation back once it is lost.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A reputation, like fine porcelain, may be the labour of a lifetime to shape yet the work of an instant to shatter — and once broken, no amount of remorse can make it whole again. （议论文·比喻警世）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: like fine porcelain 明喻贯穿 + a lifetime to shape yet an instant to shatter 时间对比 + 破折号补充 once broken 强化不可逆
