classPractice.answer: what has upset you so much
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】考点:what 引导宾语从句作 tell 的宾语,从句主语 what,谓语用现在完成时 has upset,so much 作程度状语。

classPractice.question: He was so ____ (upset) that, at first, he wanted to keep the terrible news a secret.
classPractice.note: 考点:so + adj. + that 结构中 upset 作形容词表"难过的",形态不变;呼应课文原句。

classPractice.question: 引入一个外来物种可能会打破整个生态系统的脆弱平衡。Introducing a foreign species can ____ ____ ____ of an entire ecosystem.
classPractice.note: 考点:动词 upset + the balance 表"打破平衡",体现 upset"扰乱"义。

classPractice.question: 选词填空(词性判断)：In the biggest ____ (upset) of the tournament, the unranked boy beat the champion.（判断此处 upset 作何词性）
classPractice.answer: upset（名词，意为"爆冷、意外结果"）
classPractice.note: 考点:冠词 the biggest + of 结构中 upset 为名词,指"爆冷、意外结果",非形容词。

translation: 具有(特质)；拥有；占据，支配，控制
original_sentence: 25 30 35 40 me than in others, a sense which I once possessed in the greatest perfection …” Even in his darkest moments, however, Beethoven never abandoned hope.
readingExamples: 25 30 35 40 me than in others, a sense which I once possessed in the greatest perfection …” Even in his darkest moments, however, Beethoven never abandoned hope.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to have or own something, especially something valuable or a particular quality
(2) vt. (of a feeling or idea) to take control of someone's mind or influence their behaviour strongly
(3) vt. (formal or literary) to have a strong effect on someone as if controlling them; to seize

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】支配，控制，攫住（of a feeling 情绪支配某人 = seize）
uncommonMeanings.example: A wave of fear possessed her. 一阵恐惧攫住了她。（课件·possess 表情绪支配 = seize sb）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (情绪、念头)支配，控制，使着魔
uncommonMeanings.example: A sudden, reckless courage possessed her, and before fear could return, she had already stepped forward to shield the trembling child from the crowd. （读后续写·瞬间勇气·被情绪驱使）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (委婉/惊讶)使……做出反常之举，鬼迷心窍（what possessed sb. to do sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: Whatever possessed you to sell the very violin your grandfather left you? she gasped, unable to believe her ears. （读后续写·质问·反常之举）

posExamples.sentence: Though he possessed neither wealth nor fame, the old carpenter possessed something far rarer — an unshakeable serenity that drew people to his humble workshop. （读后续写·人物品质）
I believe every candidate for this leadership role should possess not only academic excellence but also empathy, integrity, and the courage to serve. （应用文·竞选演讲）
Those who possess a growth mindset regard every obstacle not as a wall but as a door waiting to be pushed open. （议论文·思维方式）
As the ancient scroll unrolled before us, we realised it possessed a quiet power to summon a vanished world back to life. （读后续写·文物/历史）

wordForms.noun: possession（拥有；财产；着迷）; possessor（拥有者）
wordForms.adjective: possessed（着魔的）; possessive（占有欲强的）

idioms.example: She was possessed of a rare gift for turning strangers into friends within minutes. （读后续写·人物魅力）
He worked like a man possessed through the night, determined to finish the mural before the exhibition opened at dawn. （读后续写·忘我拼搏）

idioms.idiom: possession is nine-tenths of the law
idioms.translation: 占有者在法律上占九分优势(谚)
idioms.example: The two families quarrelled endlessly over the old cottage, each insisting that possession is nine-tenths of the law. （议论文·产权/引谚）

collocations.phrase: possess a sense of humour（课件）
collocations.example: The gallery possesses a number of the artist's early works. 这家画廊藏有那位画家的一些早期作品。（课件·vt. to own sth 拥有物品、特质）
She was possessed of exceptional power of concentration. 她有高超的专注能力。（课件·be possessed of = 具有）

collocations.phrase: A wave of fear possessed sb（课件）
collocations.translation: 【课件】一阵恐惧支配 / 攫住某人（= seize sb）
collocations.example: A wave of fear possessed her. 一阵恐惧攫住了她。（课件·vt. 支配，控制 = seize sb）

collocations.phrase: be possessed by a desire（课件）
collocations.translation: 【课件】被一种欲望支配（着魔于……）
collocations.example: I was possessed by a desire to tell her everything. 我有一种想把一切都告诉她的强烈冲动。（课件·be possessed by 被支配）

collocations.translation: 【课件】私人物品（possession 意为"财产"时常用复数 = belongings）
collocations.example: The ring is one of her most treasured possessions. 这只戒指是她最珍贵的财产之一。（课件·possession 作"财产"义常用复数）

collocations.translation: 【课件】拥有某物（= have sth in one's possession）
collocations.example: The gang was caught in possession of stolen goods. 这伙人被逮住，人赃俱获。（课件·主语为拥有者）

collocations.phrase: in the possession of sb（课件）
collocations.translation: 【课件】在某人手中，由某人掌握（= sth be in the possession of sb）
collocations.example: Those documents are now in the possession of the Guardian. 这些文件现在由《卫报》掌握。（课件·主语为被拥有物,与 in possession of 主语相反）
She had taken possession of the sofa. 她占据了那张沙发。A wave of fear took possession of me. 一阵恐惧攫住了我。（课件·take possession of = 占有）

collocations.phrase: sth come into one's possession（课件）
collocations.example: The book came into my possession. 这本书为我所得。（课件·come into one's possession）

collocations.translation: 具有某种品质 / 才能 / 技能
collocations.example: To lead others, one must first possess the quality of listening more than one speaks. （议论文·领导力）

collocations.phrase: possess the ability / power to do sth
collocations.translation: 有能力 / 力量做某事
collocations.example: Words possess the power to heal wounds that no medicine can reach. （议论文·语言的力量）
The interns quickly discovered that possessing knowledge and applying it wisely are two very different things. （议论文·知行）

collocations.translation: 被恐惧 / 愤怒支配（着魔于……）
collocations.example: Possessed by fear, the young soldier froze — until the memory of his sister's smile gave him the strength to move. （读后续写·心理挣扎）

collocations.phrase: what possessed sb. to do sth
collocations.translation: 什么让某人（鬼迷心窍）做出……
collocations.example: She could not imagine what had possessed him to abandon so promising a career on a mere whim. （读后续写/口语·惊讶质问）
She possessed a natural charm that put even the most nervous newcomer instantly at ease. （读后续写·人物形象）
He gave all that he possessed to rebuild the village school, keeping nothing back for himself. （读后续写·无私奉献）
Little by little, through years of quiet study, she possessed herself of a wisdom no diploma could confer. （议论文·自我修养）
Stripped of all his worldly possessions, the traveller discovered that his richest treasure was the kindness of strangers. （读后续写·感悟）

synonyms.example: The family had owned the little bakery for three generations, and its scent was woven into every childhood memory. （读后续写·家族传承）
synonyms.usage: 最普通，强调法律所有权，多指具体财物;possess 更正式，且可用于抽象品质，语气更书面

synonyms.example: She holds a firm belief that honesty, however costly, is always the wiser path. （议论文·信念）
synonyms.usage: 常与 belief/view/record/position 搭配，指持有观点或职位;possess 更强调"具备"某种内在特质

synonyms.example: The ancient city boasts a history stretching back over two thousand years. （应用文·景点介绍）
synonyms.usage: 褒义,主语常为地点/机构,含引以为豪之意;possess 中性，可褒可贬，适用范围更广

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·possession 一组高频短语辨主语（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: be in possession of sth（主语=拥有者:拥有某物）= have sth in one's possession ↔ sth be in the possession of sb（主语=被拥有物:由某人掌握）；take possession of / come into one's possession
advancedExpressions.example: 老师对照板书:主语是人用 in possession of（She is in possession of the key）;主语是物用 in the possession of（The key is in the possession of her）。两者主语正好相反,是语法填空、一句多译高频考点。

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·possess 主动与被动两面
advancedExpressions.expression: 主动 possess sth（拥有品质/才能）↔ 被动 be possessed by sth（被情绪支配、着魔）；be possessed of sth（正式:具有）
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书:possess 后跟宾语="拥有";被 be possessed by 情绪="被支配、着魔"。She possessed great courage, yet in that instant she was possessed by a fear she could not name. （同词的主动"拥有"与被动"被支配"对照）

advancedExpressions.expression: possess(v.) → possession(n. 拥有;财产;着迷) → possessor(n. 拥有者) → possessed(adj. 着魔的) → possessive(adj. 占有欲强的;语法"所有格的")
advancedExpressions.example: 老师提醒双 s 拼写别漏:posse-ss。A possessive child guards his possessions as if possessed. （possessive / possessions / possessed 同族同现,记双 s）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·what possessed sb. to do sth
advancedExpressions.expression: What possessed sb. to do sth?（到底是什么让某人做出如此反常之事?——表惊讶、不解）
advancedExpressions.example: 老师点出这是地道口语强调句:possess 在此="驱使、鬼迷心窍"。What on earth possessed you to hand in a blank paper? the teacher asked in disbelief. （what...possess...to do 表难以置信的质问）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. possessed a rare ... that ...
advancedExpressions.example: He possessed a rare stillness that seemed to calm every room he entered, as though anxiety simply could not survive in his presence. （possess a rare + 定语从句,凝练刻画人物）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. possesses the qualities essential to ...
advancedExpressions.example: In my view, she possesses all the qualities essential to a first-rate team leader: vision, patience, and unfailing fairness. （推荐信列举式高级表达）

advancedExpressions.expression: to possess ... is one thing; to ... is another
advancedExpressions.example: To possess talent is one thing; to nurture it through years of discipline is another entirely. （one thing...another 对比,深化论点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He had a special kind of calm.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: He possessed a rare and quiet calm — the kind that gathers around a person like still water, so that even in the fiercest storm, those beside him felt strangely safe. （读后续写·人物魅力）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: possess 替换 have + 破折号补充比喻(still water) + so that 结果状语渲染感染力 + 环境反衬(fiercest storm)

sentenceUpgrade.original: A good leader should have many good qualities.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm conviction that a truly effective leader must possess not merely competence, but the deeper virtues of empathy, humility, and unwavering integrity. （应用文·演讲/建议）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm conviction that 正式主句 + possess 替换 have + not merely...but 递进结构 + 三名词并列(empathy, humility, integrity)增强气势

classPractice.question: When you get out of the taxi, make sure that none of your ____ (possess) are left behind.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】考点:possession 意为"财产、私人物品"时用复数 possessions;none of your possessions 后接复数名词。

classPractice.question: It seems that we value what we are trying to get more than what we ____ (possess) right now.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】考点:what 引导的宾语从句中作谓语,主语 we 为第一人称、时间状语 right now 用一般现在时,故用原形 possess。

classPractice.question: Right after Erin took ____ (possess) of my wallet on the bus, she posted a picture of my driver's license to an online forum, trying to see if anyone knew me. (2019 天津)
classPractice.note: 【课件原题·2019 天津】考点:固定短语 take possession of sth"占有某物",possess 需变名词 possession。

classPractice.question: 据我所知，他拥有一个大公司。① As far as I know, he is ____ a large company.（用 possession 短语,主语为人）② As far as I know, a large company is ____ him.（用 possession 短语,主语为物）③ As far as I know, he ____ a large company.（用动词 possess）
classPractice.answer: ① in possession of ② in the possession of ③ possesses
classPractice.note: 【课件原题·一句多译】考点:①主语是人 he,用 be in possession of sth;②主语是物 a large company,用 be in the possession of sb;③直接用动词 possess,第三人称单数加 -es。

classPractice.question: Beethoven once ____ (possess) a sense of hearing more perfect than most people's, which made his deafness all the more painful.
classPractice.note: 考点:possess 作"拥有"义的及物动词,依时间状语 once 用一般过去时。

classPractice.question: 老师难以置信地问：到底是什么让你交了一张白卷？The teacher asked in disbelief, "____ ____ ____ to hand in a blank paper?"
classPractice.note: 考点:固定句式 What possessed sb. to do sth 表"什么让某人鬼迷心窍/做出反常之举"。

classPractice.question: 词形选择：____ (Possessed / Possessive) by fear, the young soldier froze, unable to take a single step.
classPractice.note: 考点:be possessed by 表"被(情绪)支配",此处过去分词短语作状语用 Possessed;possessive 意为"占有欲强的",不合语境。

translation: 中止，放弃，不再有；抛弃，遗弃
original_sentence: You might need to abandon logical thinking to discover its true inner beauty.
readingExamples: You might need to abandon logical thinking to discover its true inner beauty.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to stop doing an activity or plan, especially before it is finished, because of problems or difficulties
(2) vt. to leave a person, place, or thing permanently, especially when you have a responsibility to stay
(3) vt. to give up completely a belief, hope, or way of behaving
(4) n. (formal) a state of complete lack of self-control or restraint

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】被抛弃的，废弃的（abandoned = deserted）
uncommonMeanings.example: an abandoned car / house 废弃的汽车 / 房屋。（课件·abandoned 作形容词,同义 deserted）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 放纵，纵情，无拘无束
uncommonMeanings.example: As the drums quickened, the villagers threw themselves into the dance with wild abandon, their laughter rising like sparks into the night sky. （读后续写·节日狂欢·尽情释放）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使(自己)沉溺于，纵情于(常用 abandon oneself to)
uncommonMeanings.example: For one afternoon she abandoned herself to the simple joy of painting, forgetting every worry that had shadowed her days. （读后续写·自我疗愈·忘我）

posExamples.sentence: Halfway up the treacherous slope, the exhausted climbers were forced to abandon their attempt, though the summit gleamed tantalisingly close through the swirling mist. （读后续写·探险受阻）
I strongly urge our school never to abandon its long tradition of community service, for it is precisely this spirit that defines who we are. （应用文·建议信/倡议）
Those who abandon their principles at the first sign of hardship rarely achieve anything of lasting worth. （议论文·坚守原则）
No matter how fierce the storm grew, the old captain refused to abandon the sinking ship until every last passenger had reached the lifeboats. （读后续写·责任担当）

wordForms.noun: abandonment（放弃；抛弃）; abandon（放纵）

idioms.example: The children splashed through the puddles with reckless abandon, utterly indifferent to their soaked shoes and their mother's calls. （读后续写·童趣）

idioms.translation: 弃船(逃生)；(比喻)抽身退出，弃之不顾
idioms.example: Just as the project neared collapse, several members chose to abandon ship, but she stayed on, determined to see it through. （读后续写·坚守）

collocations.example: Even in his darkest moments, however, Beethoven never abandoned hope. 然而，即使在那些最晦暗的时刻，贝多芬都不曾放弃希望。（课件·课文原句）
They abandoned the match because of rain. 因为下雨，他们中止了比赛。（课件·vt. 中止、放弃未完成之事）
I don't think that John would abandon his friends if they were in trouble. 我不认为约翰会抛弃他遇到麻烦的朋友。（课件·vt. 抛弃、遗弃）
He abandoned himself to despair. 他陷入绝望。（课件·abandon oneself to = 沉溺、陷入某种情绪）

collocations.phrase: be abandoned to the care of sb（课件）
collocations.translation: 【课件】被抛给某人照料（被遗弃）
collocations.example: The study showed a deep fear among the elderly of being abandoned to the care of strangers. 研究显示老年人深深害怕被抛给陌生人照料。（课件·被动·被遗弃）
They took shelter in an abandoned house at the edge of the village. 他们在村口一栋废弃的房子里避雨。（课件·abandoned adj. 被抛弃的、废弃的 = deserted）
You might need to abandon logical thinking to discover its true inner beauty. （课文原句·欣赏音乐时或需放下逻辑）

collocations.translation: 放纵地，无拘无束地，尽情地
collocations.example: As the drums quickened, the villagers danced with wild abandon, their laughter rising like sparks into the night sky. （读后续写·节日狂欢·尽情释放）

collocations.phrase: abandon a plan / an attempt / an idea
collocations.translation: 放弃计划 / 尝试 / 想法
collocations.example: Rather than abandon her dream after the rejection, she reshaped it into something even bolder. （读后续写·逆境奋起）
A person who will abandon his principles for profit can never be truly trusted. （议论文·诚信）

collocations.translation: 对某人见死不救，弃之不顾
collocations.example: How could we abandon those flood victims to their fate when a single boat could carry them to safety? （议论文·社会责任）
The abandoned village, its windows like hollow eyes, seemed to hold its breath as the travellers passed through. （读后续写·环境描写）
Standing alone at the empty station, the boy felt utterly abandoned, until a warm hand rested gently on his shoulder. （读后续写·孤独与救赎）
True leaders do not abandon a worthy cause simply because the road grows steep. （议论文·担当）
Even trapped in the darkness of the collapsed mine, the workers refused to abandon hope, tapping steadily on the pipes for rescuers to hear. （读后续写·绝境求生）
He abandoned himself to grief for a single night, then rose at dawn resolved to honour his friend by living fully. （读后续写·由悲转坚）

synonyms.example: He would never desert a friend in need, whatever the cost to himself. （读后续写·忠诚）
synonyms.usage: 强调背弃责任、临阵脱逃，含道德谴责;abandon 更中性，适用范围更广(计划、地点、人皆可)

synonyms.example: Never give up on a goal simply because it takes longer than you hoped. （应用文·励志）
synonyms.usage: 最口语、最常用;abandon 更正式书面，且含"半途丢下、不再管"的意味，语气更重

synonyms.example: She forsook the comforts of city life to teach in a remote mountain school. （读后续写·奉献）
synonyms.usage: 文学、庄重色彩最浓，多指主动舍弃所珍视之物;日常写作用 abandon 更自然

advancedExpressions.expression: abandon sth（放弃计划/希望/原则）→ abandon oneself to sth（沉溺于）→ with abandon（名词:放纵地、尽情地）
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书三档:及物动词"放弃"最常考,abandon oneself to=沉溺,介词短语 with abandon=尽情地。He abandoned all caution and threw himself into the dance with abandon. （同词动词义与名词义 with abandon 对照）

advancedExpressions.expression: abandon(v.) → abandonment(n. 放弃;抛弃) → abandoned(adj. 被遗弃的;放纵的) → abandon(n. 放纵)
advancedExpressions.example: 老师提醒:abandoned 兼有"被遗弃的"(an abandoned village)与"放纵的"(abandoned laughter)两义。The abandoned child, years later, danced through life with a joyful abandon no hardship could dim. （abandoned 与名词 abandon 同现,双义对照）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. refused to abandon ...
advancedExpressions.example: Even as his strength failed, he refused to abandon the search, clawing through the rubble with bleeding fingers for the faintest cry. （refuse to abandon 凸显意志 + 动作细节）

advancedExpressions.expression: we must never abandon our commitment to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Whatever challenges lie ahead, we must never abandon our commitment to protecting this precious environment for generations to come. （倡议信结尾呼吁）

advancedExpressions.expression: to abandon ... is to abandon ...
advancedExpressions.example: To abandon our curiosity is to abandon the very engine of human progress. （to...is to... 对称句,警句式论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The children played happily in the rain.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The children danced through the summer rain with pure abandon, their upturned faces glowing with a joy so unguarded that even the passing strangers could not help but smile. （读后续写·童趣狂欢）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: with abandon 名词用法替换 happily + 动作细节(upturned faces, glowing) + so...that 结果状语传染情绪 + 旁观者反应烘托

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not give up our traditions.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It would be a grave mistake to abandon the time-honoured traditions that have bound our community together, for once such roots are severed, no wealth on earth can restore them. （议论文·文化传承）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It would be a grave mistake to 评价句式 + abandon 替换 give up + time-honoured 高级形容词 + for 引出因果 + 隐喻(roots severed)强化论证

classPractice.question: Feeling frustrated, I found myself abandoning myself to ____ (play) computer games.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】考点:abandon oneself to 中 to 为介词,后接动名词 playing 表"沉溺于打电脑游戏"。

classPractice.question: He owned a farm, which looked almost ____ (abandon).
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】考点:系动词 looked 后作表语,农场"被废弃",用过去分词形容词 abandoned"废弃的"（= deserted）。

classPractice.question: 听到这个坏消息，她沉浸在悲痛中。（用 abandon oneself to）
classPractice.answer: Hearing the bad news, she abandoned herself to sadness.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题·仿写】考点:abandon oneself to sth"沉溺、陷入某种情绪",oneself 与主语 she 一致用 herself,现在分词短语 Hearing... 作时间/原因状语。

classPractice.question: To appreciate the music fully, you might need to ____ (abandon) logical thinking and simply feel.
classPractice.note: 考点:情态动词 need to 后接动词原形 abandon,表"放弃";呼应课文原句。

classPractice.question: 孩子们不顾湿透的鞋子，尽情地在水坑里嬉戏。The children splashed through the puddles ____ ____, indifferent to their soaked shoes.
classPractice.note: 考点:名词性短语 with abandon 意为"放纵地、尽情地",作方式状语。

classPractice.question: 选词填空(abandon / desert)：A true friend would never ____ you in your hour of need.（择更强调背弃责任的词）
classPractice.note: 考点:两词此处均可;desert 更强调临阵脱逃、道德谴责,abandon 更中性通用。

translation: 突然，忽地
original_sentence: Zhang’s amazing artistic technique is apparent all across the scroll.
readingExamples: Zhang’s amazing artistic technique is apparent all across the scroll.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. happening quickly and unexpectedly; suddenly and without warning
(2) phr. used to mark an abrupt change from a previous, usually calmer, state of affairs

posExamples.sentence: The forest lay in perfect silence, and then, all of a sudden, a deafening crack split the air as a great pine came crashing down before our eyes. （读后续写·突发惊险）
I was calmly explaining the plan to the committee when, all of a sudden, the lights went out and the entire hall fell into an uneasy hush. （应用文·活动纪实/记叙）
Change rarely arrives all of a sudden; more often, it is the quiet accumulation of countless small choices that reshapes a life. （议论文·渐变与积累）
She had almost given up hope when, all of a sudden, a familiar voice called her name across the crowded platform, and her heart leapt. （读后续写·失而复得）

collocations.phrase: but all of a sudden ...（课文原句）
collocations.example: The first movement starts quietly, but all of a sudden the whole orchestra breaks into an energetic theme. （课文原句·乐曲第一乐章由静转急）
We were laughing over old photographs when, all of a sudden, the phone rang with news that changed everything. （读后续写·转折触发）
The path seemed endless, and then all of a sudden the trees parted to reveal a valley bathed in golden light. （读后续写·豁然开朗）

collocations.phrase: all of a sudden, everything changed
collocations.example: All of a sudden, everything changed: the crowd that had jeered moments before now rose in a roar of applause. （读后续写·逆转）

collocations.phrase: all of a sudden it dawned on sb.
collocations.example: All of a sudden it dawned on me why my grandfather had kept that worn letter for over fifty years. （读后续写·顿悟）
True mastery does not come all of a sudden but is forged through years of patient, deliberate practice. （议论文·积累）

collocations.phrase: all of a sudden the mood shifted
collocations.example: All of a sudden the mood in the room shifted from tense silence to warm, relieved laughter. （读后续写·气氛转变）

synonyms.example: Suddenly, a gust of wind snatched the papers from his hands and scattered them across the busy street. （读后续写·突发）
synonyms.usage: 单个副词,最常用最简洁,句首/句中位置灵活;all of a sudden 是口语化短语(=suddenly),语气更生动、更有画面停顿感,常配 when 从句

synonyms.example: Out of the blue, an email arrived offering her the very opportunity she had long stopped dreaming about. （读后续写·意外惊喜）
synonyms.usage: 强调完全出人意料、毫无征兆,多指令人惊喜或震惊之事;all of a sudden 更侧重动作的骤然发生,不必强调"没预兆"

synonyms.example: All at once, the memories she had buried for years came flooding back. （读后续写·记忆涌现）
synonyms.usage: 既可表"突然",也可表"同时(一齐)";表"突然"时与 all of a sudden 近义,但 all at once 更强调瞬间的整体涌现

synonyms.example: In an instant the calm lake turned to chaos as a squall tore across the water. （读后续写·骤变）
synonyms.usage: 强调时间之短、变化之快,侧重"一瞬完成";all of a sudden 侧重"意外发生",可与之互补使用

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·表"突然"功能
advancedExpressions.expression: all of a sudden = suddenly ≈ all at once ≈ out of the blue ≈ without warning（突然,毫无征兆）
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书一组"突然"家族:最口语生动的是 all of a sudden 和 all at once,最书面的是 without warning。All of a sudden — without any warning at all — the sky split open with lightning. （两个"突然"表达叠用,强化骤然感）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·all of a sudden 作插入状语
advancedExpressions.expression: ..., when all of a sudden, + 主谓（前平静铺垫 + when 引出突发转折,续写黄金句式）
advancedExpressions.example: 老师强调:此处 when 不译"当",而是"就在这时",前用逗号,后接突发事件——续写制造波澜的利器。The campfire crackled softly, when all of a sudden a pair of glowing eyes appeared at the edge of the dark. （when all of a sudden 承接平静、引爆惊险）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., when all of a sudden ...
advancedExpressions.example: The night was calm and the campfire crackled softly, when all of a sudden a pair of glowing eyes appeared at the edge of the darkness. （用平静铺垫 + when all of a sudden 制造惊险转折）

advancedExpressions.expression: everything was going smoothly until, all of a sudden, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Everything was going smoothly until, all of a sudden, a power failure plunged the entire exhibition into darkness. （记叙类应用文,推进事件）

advancedExpressions.expression: success does not arrive all of a sudden; rather, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Success does not arrive all of a sudden; rather, it is the harvest of seeds sown quietly, season after season. （否定+rather 纠偏,配合比喻升华）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Suddenly the door opened.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The corridor was steeped in an uneasy stillness when, all of a sudden, the heavy door swung open with a groan, and a figure stepped out of the shadows. （读后续写·悬念）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 环境铺垫(steeped in stillness)蓄势 + when all of a sudden 转折 + 拟声细节(swung open with a groan) + figure out of shadows 制造悬念

sentenceUpgrade.original: Then I understood why he had done it.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: And then, all of a sudden, it all became clear — every strange thing he had done was, in truth, a quiet act of love I had been too blind to see. （读后续写·顿悟收束）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: all of a sudden 强化顿悟时刻 + 破折号引出揭示 + it all became clear 顶点 + too...to 结构表遗憾自省，升华情感

classPractice.question: 乐曲第一乐章开始时很安静，但突然整个乐队奏起了激昂的主题。The movement starts quietly, but ____ ____ ____ ____ the whole orchestra breaks into an energetic theme.
classPractice.note: 考点:固定短语 all of a sudden 作状语表"突然";呼应课文原句。

classPractice.question: 改写为同义句：Suddenly, the lights went out and the hall fell silent. → ____ ____ ____ ____, the lights went out and the hall fell silent.
classPractice.note: 考点:all of a sudden = suddenly,是其习语式同义表达,可置于句首。

classPractice.question: 成功不会突然降临；相反，它是日积月累静静播种的收获。（用 all of a sudden 和 rather）
classPractice.answer: Success does not come / arrive all of a sudden; rather, it is the harvest of seeds sown quietly, day after day.
classPractice.note: 考点:not...all of a sudden; rather... 用"否定突然 + rather 纠偏"结构强调积累。

translation: 管弦乐队
original_sentence: The first movement starts quietly, but all of a sudden the whole orchestra breaks into an energetic theme.
readingExamples: The first movement starts quietly, but all of a sudden the whole orchestra breaks into an energetic theme.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a large group of musicians who play many different kinds of instruments together, led by a conductor
(2) n. the musicians of such a group considered collectively as a performing body
(3) n. (AmE) the ground floor of seats nearest the stage in a theatre; the stalls

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (剧院)正厅前排座位(美式英语)
uncommonMeanings.example: From their seats in the orchestra, they could see every bead of sweat on the actor's brow, every flicker of emotion the balcony crowd would surely miss. （读后续写·剧院场景·近距离观察）

posExamples.sentence: The conductor raised his baton, and for one breathless second the entire orchestra hung suspended in silence; then the strings surged forward and the hall was flooded with a river of sound. （读后续写·音乐会·画面感）
I am writing to warmly invite you to join our school orchestra, where students of every level rehearse together each week and gradually discover the joy of making music as one. （应用文·邀请信）
A symphony orchestra is a fitting metaphor for a harmonious society: each instrument keeps its own voice, yet all of them yield to a shared rhythm for the sake of a greater whole. （议论文·个体与集体）
When the timid new cellist finally found her place within the orchestra, she realised that belonging was not about standing out but about blending in at exactly the right moment. （读后续写·成长感悟）

wordForms.noun: orchestra (管弦乐队); orchestration (n. 管弦乐编曲); orchestrator (n. 策划者，编曲者)
wordForms.verb: orchestrate (vt. 为管弦乐队编曲；精心策划、安排)
wordForms.other: 构词法·：orchestra(乐队)→ orchestr- + -al = orchestral(形容词，管弦乐的)；→ orchestra + -ate = orchestrate(动词，编曲/策划)。易混：orchestra 重音在第一音节 /ˈɔːkɪstrə/，注意 -ch- 读 /k/ 而非 /tʃ/。orchestration (n. 管弦乐编曲); orchestrator (n. 策划者)

collocations.example: A symphony orchestra of nearly a hundred players filled the hall with sound. 近百人的交响乐团让整个大厅充满了乐声。
The young maestro conducted the orchestra without a single glance at the score. 年轻的大师指挥乐队时没看一眼乐谱。
She has played the cello in the orchestra for ten years. 她在乐团里拉大提琴已经十年了。

collocations.phrase: the (whole) orchestra breaks into / strikes up sth
collocations.example: The music starts quietly, but all of a sudden the whole orchestra breaks into an energetic theme. 乐曲开头很安静，但突然整个乐队奏起充满活力的主题。（课文原句词块）

collocations.translation: 室内乐团 / 校乐队 / 青年乐团
collocations.example: He got his first taste of the stage in the school orchestra. 他在校乐队里第一次尝到了登台的滋味。
The musicians tuned their instruments down in the orchestra pit. 乐师们在乐池里给乐器调音。
The film's finale was backed by a full orchestra. 影片的终场由完整编制的乐团配乐。
Joining the youth orchestra transformed a shy boy who once feared the classroom into a confident performer who could face a thousand faces without flinching. （读后续写·蜕变）
Unlike the thunderous symphony orchestra, the chamber orchestra wove a delicate, intimate sound that seemed meant for a single listener. （议论文·对比）

synonyms.example: The small jazz ensemble filled the café with a warmth that no recording could ever capture. （读后续写·氛围）
synonyms.usage: 泛指任何规模的合奏团体(可小可大),orchestra 特指有弦、管、打击乐器完整编制的大型管弦乐团

synonyms.translation: 乐队(尤指流行/军乐/管乐)
synonyms.example: The marching band swept down the avenue, their brass instruments blazing like small suns in the morning light. （读后续写·游行）
synonyms.usage: band 多指流行乐队、军乐队或管乐队,不含弦乐主体;orchestra 以弦乐为核心、规模更大、演奏古典曲目

advancedExpressions.expression: the whole orchestra breaks into / strikes up / swells into ...
advancedExpressions.example: The whole orchestra broke into a triumphant crescendo, and in that swelling wave of sound she felt her courage rising. （break into 奏起 / strike up 开始演奏 / swell into 渐强至……，续写高潮段常用）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as an orchestra thrives on ..., so too does ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as an orchestra thrives on the disciplined cooperation of many voices, so too does a nation flourish when its diverse citizens play in harmony. （议论文·个体与集体的经典类比）

advancedExpressions.expression: the whole orchestra broke into ..., and ...
advancedExpressions.example: The whole orchestra broke into a triumphant crescendo, and in that swelling wave of sound she felt her long-buried courage rising to meet it. （by that swelling wave 用音乐意象承载情感,续写高潮段）

advancedExpressions.expression: we sincerely welcome you to become part of our orchestra, where ...
advancedExpressions.example: We sincerely welcome you to become part of our school orchestra, where friendship is tuned as carefully as every instrument and no talent is ever left unheard. （招募信,双关 tuned 呼应音乐主题）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as an orchestra thrives on ..., so too does ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as an orchestra thrives on the disciplined cooperation of many voices, so too does a nation flourish when its diverse citizens play in harmony toward a common goal.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The orchestra played and it was beautiful.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the orchestra swelled into the final movement, wave upon wave of sound washed over the hall, and tears she had not known she was holding slipped quietly down her cheeks. （读后续写·情感+画面）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: swell into 动态动词 + wave upon wave 叠词渲染 + tears she had not known she was holding 后置定语暗写压抑情感 + 感官描写

sentenceUpgrade.original: The school has an orchestra that students can join.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Our school takes great pride in its orchestra, a vibrant community in which students of all backgrounds rehearse side by side, growing not only as musicians but as a family. （应用文·介绍信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: takes great pride in 正式表达 + 同位语补充说明 + in which 定语从句 + not only...but 递进 + 情感升华

classPractice.question: The music starts quietly, but all of a sudden the whole ____ (orchestra) breaks into an energetic theme.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；orchestra 作可数名词，前接 the whole 指整支乐队

classPractice.question: 选词填空 (orchestra / orchestral / orchestrate)：The composer chose to ____ the folk tune for a full symphony orchestra.
classPractice.note: 词族辨析：动词 orchestrate(编曲) vs 名词 orchestra vs 形容词 orchestral；此处需动词

classPractice.question: 加入学校乐团彻底改变了这个曾经害羞的男孩。(orchestra)
classPractice.answer: Joining the school orchestra completely transformed / changed the once-shy boy.
classPractice.note: join the orchestra 加入乐团；动名词短语作主语

translation: 绝望的；不顾一切的；极需要的；极严重的
original_sentence: The next two movements are full of desperate lows and uplifting highs which perhaps reflect both his suffering and his strong will to fight it.
readingExamples: The next two movements are full of desperate lows and uplifting highs which perhaps reflect both his suffering and his strong will to fight it.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. feeling or showing that you have little hope and are ready to do anything without worrying about danger
(2) adj. needing or wanting something very much (desperate for sth / to do sth)
(3) adj. (of a situation) so bad that you feel worried and without hope; extremely serious or dangerous
(4) adj. (of an action) tried when everything else has failed, and unlikely to succeed; done as a last resort

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 极需要的,渴求的(desperate for)
uncommonMeanings.example: After three days lost in the wilderness, they were desperate for a single sip of clean water, and the distant glint of a stream set their cracked lips trembling with hope. （读后续写·求生·极度渴求）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (情况)极其严重、危急的
uncommonMeanings.example: The village's situation grew desperate as the floodwaters rose past the rooftops, yet still the volunteers refused to abandon a single stranded family. （读后续写·灾难·危急）

posExamples.sentence: With the flames licking at the door and no exit left, the trapped miner made one last desperate lunge toward the narrow shaft, driven by the thought of the daughter waiting at home. （读后续写·绝境·不顾一切）
I am writing on behalf of a family in our neighbourhood who are in desperate need of assistance after losing everything in the recent fire. （应用文·求助信）
Desperate measures, however dramatic they may appear, rarely solve deep-rooted problems; lasting change is born of patience and reason, not of panic. （议论文·冷静与冲动）
She was desperate to prove her doubters wrong, and each night, long after the lights of the dormitory had gone dark, she bent over her books with a fierce, unyielding resolve. （读后续写·励志·渴望证明自己）

wordForms.noun: desperation (n. 绝望；不顾一切；铤而走险)
wordForms.adverb: desperately (adv. 绝望地；拼命地；极度地)
wordForms.other: 构词法·：desperate(adj.)→ desperate + -ly = desperately(adv.)；→ desper- + -ation = desperation(n.)。同根：despair (n./v. 绝望)，注意 -sper- 源于拉丁 sperare(希望)，de-(去掉)+sper(希望)= 失去希望。易混拼写：desperate 中间是 -per-a-te，不要写成 desparate。desperately 可作程度副词 = 非常(desperately poor 赤贫)

idioms.idiom: desperate times call for desperate measures
idioms.translation: 非常时期需采取非常手段
idioms.example: The harvest had failed and winter was closing in; desperate times, the old farmer muttered, call for desperate measures, and so he set out on foot to the distant city for help. （读后续写·困境·谚语引用）

collocations.example: The next two movements are full of desperate lows and uplifting highs which perhaps reflect both his suffering and his strong will to fight it. 接下来的两个乐章充满了绝望的低谷和令人振奋的高潮。（课件·课文原句）
I heard sounds of a desperate struggle in the next room. 我听到隔壁传来拼命挣扎的声音。（课件·adj. 拼命的、不顾一切的）

collocations.translation: 【课件】铤而走险的办法，不顾一切的手段
collocations.example: His increasing financial difficulties forced him to take desperate measures. 日益加重的经济困难迫使他采取铤而走险的办法。（课件·take desperate measures）

collocations.phrase: in desperate need of sth（课件）
collocations.example: I decided not to abandon John when he was in desperate need of help. 约翰极需帮助时，我决定不抛弃他。（课件·极其需要）

collocations.phrase: a desperate shortage of sth（课件）
collocations.example: a desperate shortage of clean water 清洁水的极度短缺。（课件·desperate 表"极其需要、极严重"）
The refugees were desperate for food and shelter. 难民们极度渴望得到食物和栖身之所。（课件·want sth very much 极想、渴望）

collocations.phrase: be desperate to do sth（课件）
collocations.example: She was desperate to see her family again after the long separation. 长久分离后她极度渴望再见到家人。（课件·be desperate to do）

collocations.phrase: so desperate for sth that ...（课件）
collocations.example: He was so desperate for a job that he would have done anything. 他太想找份工作了，什么事都愿意做。（课件·so...that + desperate for）

collocations.phrase: a desperate attempt / effort / bid (to do sth)
collocations.example: He dived in in a desperate attempt to save the drowning boy. 他跳进水里，孤注一掷地想救溺水的男孩。
A minor delay had spiralled into a desperate situation. 小小的延误演变成了危急的处境。

collocations.translation: 变得绝望 / 铤而走险
collocations.example: As days passed without rescue, even the calmest of them grew desperate. 一天天过去仍无人来救，连最镇定的人都开始绝望。
A desperate cry for help pierced the fog, and without thinking twice, the sailors turned their boat toward the darkness. （读后续写·营救）
Born into desperate poverty, she nonetheless refused to let her circumstances define the size of her dreams. （议论文·逆境成才）
After the long march, the soldiers were desperate for water. 长途行军后，士兵们极度渴望喝到水。

collocations.translation: 极想做某事，不顾一切要做某事
collocations.example: She was desperate to prove that she deserved the chance. 她拼命想证明自己配得上这个机会。
The rural school is in desperate need of books. 这所乡村学校急需图书。

synonyms.example: Just when the search seemed utterly hopeless, a faint light flickered on the far ridge and rekindled their fading spirits. （读后续写·转机）
synonyms.usage: hopeless 强调客观上毫无希望的状态,较被动;desperate 强调因绝望而愿意冒险、拼命行动,带主动性和情绪张力

synonyms.example: The mother made frantic phone calls one after another, her voice cracking as the minutes crawled past. （读后续写·焦急）
synonyms.usage: frantic 侧重因焦虑而慌乱、忙乱的外在状态;desperate 更强调因走投无路而孤注一掷的决心

synonyms.example: The eager young intern volunteered for every task, hungry to prove that she belonged. （应用文·个人陈述）
synonyms.usage: eager 是中性偏积极的热切渴望;desperate for 程度更深、更迫切,常含焦虑或走投无路之意

advancedExpressions.expression: desperate(adj. 绝望的/拼命的/极需要的) → desperately(adv. 绝望地、拼命地；程度副词=非常) → desperation(n. 绝望；拼命)
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书课件例:desperately ill / unhappy / lonely（极其病重/不快/孤独,desperately 作程度副词=非常）;There was a note of desperation in his voice. 他的声音里带着一丝绝望。（a note of desperation 固定说法）

advancedExpressions.expression: be desperate for sth / be desperate to do sth / in desperate need of sth
advancedExpressions.example: Stranded on the mountainside, they were desperate for warmth, desperate to find any shelter, and in desperate need of rescue. （三个高频结构串联，for + 名词，to + 动词，need of + 名词）

advancedExpressions.expression: driven by a desperate ..., sb. did ...
advancedExpressions.example: Driven by a desperate determination she scarcely recognised as her own, she flung open the door and stepped into the storm. （用 driven by a desperate... 作状语前置,凸显内在驱动力,续写高潮段）

advancedExpressions.expression: however desperate ... may seem / be, ...
advancedExpressions.example: However desperate a crisis may seem, clear-headed cooperation, rather than reckless panic, is what turns the tide. （however + adj. 引导让步状语从句，形容词提前，议论文常用）

advancedExpressions.expression: families in desperate need are counting on ...
advancedExpressions.example: Families in desperate need are counting on our collective kindness; even the smallest donation can rekindle a hope that hardship has all but extinguished. （倡议书结尾呼吁,rekindle a hope 意象化）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He really wanted to win and tried very hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Desperate to prove that his years of quiet sacrifice had not been in vain, he threw himself into training with a ferocity that startled even his coach. （读后续写·励志·心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Desperate to do 形容词短语前置作状语 + that 从句补充动机 + with a ferocity that... 后置定语 + startled even his coach 侧面烘托

sentenceUpgrade.original: The people needed help badly after the disaster.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In the wake of the disaster, countless families found themselves in desperate need of shelter, food and, above all, a reason to believe that tomorrow might yet be kinder than today. （应用文·求助信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: In the wake of 正式短语开头 + found themselves 被动困境 + 三项并列递进(shelter, food, above all a reason) + 情感升华收尾

classPractice.question: After three days without food, the survivors were desperate ____ anything they could eat.
classPractice.note: be desperate for sth 极度渴望某物；注意 for 后接名词，to 后接动词原形

classPractice.question: 她拼命想在天亮前赶到医院。She was ____ ____ ____ the hospital before dawn.
classPractice.note: be desperate to do sth 极想做某事；to 后用动词原形

classPractice.question: In her ____ (desperate), she sold everything she owned to pay for her son's operation.
classPractice.note: 介词 in 后接名词；in desperation 绝望地/走投无路地。名词形式 desperation

translation: 让人振奋的，鼓舞人心的
original_sentence: It has an uplifting message about the determination to work hard towards your goals.
readingExamples: It has an uplifting message about the determination to work hard towards your goals.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. making you feel happier, more hopeful, or more positive about life
(2) adj. (of music, a story, a message, etc.) inspiring you and raising your spirits
(3) adj. morally or spiritually elevating; encouraging you to be a better person

posExamples.sentence: As the final note of the anthem faded, an uplifting warmth spread through the crowd, and strangers who had never met turned to one another with tears and unguarded smiles. （读后续写·音乐会·情感感染）
I would highly recommend this uplifting novel to anyone in our reading club, for it reminds us, page after page, that hope can survive even the darkest of times. （应用文·推荐信）
An uplifting role model does far more than dazzle us with achievement; he quietly convinces us that the same heights lie within our own reach. （议论文·榜样的力量）
The old teacher's uplifting words stayed with her long after graduation, surfacing in her mind whenever doubt threatened to pull her under. （读后续写·师恩·长久影响）

wordForms.noun: uplift (n. 振奋；鼓舞；提升); upliftment (n. 提升，尤指社会/精神层面)
wordForms.adjective: uplifting (令人振奋的); uplifted (被提升的，振奋的)
wordForms.other: 构词法·：up-(向上) + lift(举起) = uplift(v. 使精神向上、振奋)→ uplift + -ing = uplifting(现在分词作形容词，主动含义：'令人振奋的'，修饰给人以振奋感的事物如 message/music)。对比 uplifted(过去分词，被动/状态：'受到鼓舞的'，修饰人)。upliftment (n. 提升,尤指社会/精神层面)

collocations.translation: 鼓舞人心的信息 / 故事
collocations.example: It has an uplifting message about the determination to work hard towards your goals. 它传递着关于努力追求目标之决心的鼓舞人心的信息。（课文原句词块）
The uplifting melody made even the weariest commuters walk more lightly. 振奋人心的旋律让最疲惫的上班族脚步也轻快起来。
She found it deeply uplifting to see her shy students speak up at last. 看到害羞的学生们终于开口，她深受鼓舞。
Volunteering at the shelter turned out to be the most uplifting experience of her summer, teaching her more about kindness than any textbook ever could. （读后续写·志愿·感悟）
Kind words, however small, can have an uplifting effect that ripples far beyond the moment they are spoken. （议论文·善意）

collocations.translation: 鼓舞人心的话语 / 演讲
collocations.example: With a few uplifting words, the coach transformed a demoralised team into a squad hungry to fight for every point. （读后续写·励志）
The quiet hours she spent among the mountains proved spiritually uplifting, washing away the anxieties that city life had piled upon her. （读后续写·自然疗愈）

synonyms.example: Her inspiring journey from a village clinic to a world-famous laboratory gave hope to every girl who dared to dream. （议论文·榜样）
synonyms.usage: inspiring 侧重激发人去行动、去追求目标;uplifting 侧重提升情绪、带来希望与温暖,不一定驱使行动

synonyms.translation: 令人鼓舞的,振奋人心的
synonyms.example: It was heartening to see so many young volunteers turn up on a freezing morning to clean the riverbank. （应用文·活动报道）
synonyms.usage: heartening 多用于因某事实/迹象而感到欣慰、有信心,较正式;uplifting 情感更广、更温暖,可修饰音乐、故事、经历等

synonyms.example: The teacher's encouraging nod was all he needed to raise his trembling hand and finally speak. （读后续写·课堂）
synonyms.usage: encouraging 强调给予信心、促人继续努力;uplifting 更偏整体情绪的提升与精神鼓舞

advancedExpressions.expression: an uplifting message / an uplifting effect / spiritually uplifting
advancedExpressions.example: Beneath its simple plot, the film carried an uplifting message and left the whole audience spiritually uplifted. （uplifting 修饰事物，uplifted 修饰人，一组对照）

advancedExpressions.expression: there was something deeply uplifting about ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was something deeply uplifting about that moment — the sight of a whole town rising, hand in hand, from the ruins of the storm. （there was something... about 句式含蓄抒情,续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·强调句突出精神价值
advancedExpressions.expression: what makes ... truly uplifting is not ..., but ...
advancedExpressions.example: What makes a great story truly uplifting is not its happy ending, but its honest reckoning with hardship. （what 引导主语从句 + not...but 对比，议论文点题）

advancedExpressions.expression: there was something deeply uplifting about ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was something deeply uplifting about that moment — the sight of a whole town rising, hand in hand, from the ruins of the storm. （there was something... about 句式含蓄抒情,续写升华段）

advancedExpressions.expression: I can think of no more uplifting way to ... than ...
advancedExpressions.example: I can think of no more uplifting way to begin the new term than by inviting every classmate to share the story of a person who changed their life. （倡议信,以否定比较级强化推荐）

advancedExpressions.expression: what makes ... truly uplifting is not ..., but ...
advancedExpressions.example: What makes a great story truly uplifting is not its happy ending, but its honest reckoning with hardship — for hope shines brightest against the dark.

sentenceUpgrade.original: The song made everyone feel happy and hopeful.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The song swept through the hall like a warm current, uplifting every heart it touched and leaving in its wake a quiet, stubborn hope that no hardship could easily extinguish. （读后续写·氛围+情感）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 比喻(like a warm current) + uplifting 现在分词作状语 + in its wake 后续影响 + a quiet, stubborn hope 拟人化形容 + 从句延伸

sentenceUpgrade.original: This book gives readers hope, so I recommend it.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I wholeheartedly recommend this uplifting book, for it does what only the finest literature can — it hands its readers a lantern to carry through their own darkest nights. （应用文·推荐信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: wholeheartedly recommend 正式强调 + for 引导原因 + does what only...can 强调独特性 + 隐喻(a lantern...darkest nights) 收束升华

classPractice.question: It has an ____ (uplift) message about the determination to work hard towards your goals.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；uplift 加 -ing 构成形容词，主动含义'令人振奋的'，修饰事物 message

classPractice.question: 辨析选词 (uplifting / uplifted)：After the coach's speech, every player left the room feeling ____ and ready to fight.
classPractice.note: 修饰人、表'受到鼓舞'用 uplifted(过去分词)；修饰事物、表'令人振奋'才用 uplifting

classPractice.question: 我极力向大家推荐这本鼓舞人心的书。(uplifting, recommend)
classPractice.answer: I highly / strongly recommend this uplifting book to everyone.
classPractice.note: uplifting 作定语修饰 book；recommend sth to sb

translation: n. 容易，轻易；舒适，安逸 | vi. & vt. (使)减轻，缓解
original_sentence: The music moves through technically difficult sections with ease, showing his genius as a composer.
readingExamples: The music moves through technically difficult sections with ease, showing his genius as a composer.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the state of being comfortable and free from worry, pain, or difficulty
(2) n. the quality of being easy to do; lack of difficulty (with ease)
(3) v. to make or become less severe, painful, or difficult; to relieve
(4) v. to move something slowly and carefully into a particular position

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 容易，不费力（with ease 轻松地 = easily）
uncommonMeanings.example: The music moves through technically difficult sections with ease, showing his genius as a composer. 这段音乐轻松地穿过技术难点，显示出他作为作曲家的天赋。（课文原句）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 减轻，缓解（ease the pain / pressure / tension）
uncommonMeanings.example: A single kind word did more to ease her worry than any advice. 一句善意的话比任何建议都更能缓解她的忧虑。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 小心缓慢地移动(某物)
uncommonMeanings.example: He eased the sleeping child from his shoulder onto the bed, holding his breath at every creak of the old wooden floor. （读后续写·父爱·轻柔动作）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 安逸,舒适(a life of ease)
uncommonMeanings.example: Having tasted a life of ease, he found to his surprise that comfort brought him none of the joy that struggle once had. （议论文·安逸与奋斗）

posExamples.sentence: The veteran pianist moved through the impossible passage with such ease that the audience forgot the years of blistered fingers hidden behind that effortless grace. （读后续写·音乐会·举重若轻）
I hope these small suggestions will help to ease the pressure you have been feeling and remind you that you are never facing your troubles alone. （应用文·安慰信）
Only when genuine communication replaces suspicion will the tension between the two sides finally begin to ease. （议论文·化解矛盾）
For the first time in weeks she felt a rare sense of ease settle over her, as the last exam paper slid from her fingers and the long summer stretched out ahead. （读后续写·如释重负）

wordForms.noun: ease (容易；安逸); easiness (n. 容易;安逸)
wordForms.verb: ease (vt./vi. 减轻，缓解；小心移动)
wordForms.adjective: easy; easeful (安逸的); uneasy (不安的)
wordForms.adverb: easily (adv. 容易地); uneasily (adv. 不安地)
wordForms.other: 构词法·：ease(n.容易) ↔ easy(adj.) ↔ easily(adv.)。反义：uneasy(adj. 不安的)、uneasily。小贴士：名词 ease 与介词构成大量高频短语，务必区分—with ease(轻松地) / at ease(自在，稍息) / ill at ease(不自在) / a life of ease(安逸生活)。easiness (n. 容易;安逸); uneasy (adj. 不安的)

idioms.translation: 轻松地，毫不费力地 (= easily)
idioms.example: The music moves through technically difficult sections with ease. 这段音乐轻松地驾驭了技术难点。（课文原句词块）
Something in the old gardener's gentle smile put the frightened newcomer at ease, and for the first time that day her shoulders relaxed. （读后续写·安心）
Ill at ease among the elegant guests, he clutched his glass and prayed that no one would notice his borrowed suit. （读后续写·自卑心理）
He turned his back on a life of ease to teach in a remote mountain school, and never once regretted the choice. （议论文·奉献）

collocations.example: The music moves through technically difficult sections with ease, showing his genius as a composer. 这首乐曲将技术上棘手的部分处理得轻松自如，显示出他作为作曲家的天赋。（课件·课文原句·n. 容易、轻易）
I felt completely at ease with my family. 和家人在一起我感到十分自在。（课件·n. 舒适、安逸）
We put Mary at ease during the thunderstorm by reading her stories. 雷暴期间我们给玛丽讲故事，让她安下心来。（课件·put sb at ease）
The knowledge that she wasn't the only person in this situation eased her nervousness. 得知自己并非唯一身处此境的人，缓解了她的紧张。（课件·v. 减轻、缓解）
I gave him some medicine to ease the pain. 我给了他一些药以减轻疼痛。（课件·v. to make sth less painful 减轻）
That's not difficult. I could do it with ease. 这不难，我能轻而易举地做到。（课件·with ease = easily）

collocations.phrase: ease the pain / suffering / pressure / tension
collocations.translation: 减轻痛苦 / 缓解压力紧张
collocations.example: To ease the burden on students, the school cut back on homework. 为减轻学生负担，学校减少了作业。
He chose to ease into his new role rather than rush. 他选择慢慢适应新角色，而不是操之过急。
As the rain eased off, the rescuers pressed on. 雨渐渐小了，救援人员继续前进。
Within minutes she felt completely at ease with her new classmates, as if she had known them all her life. （读后续写·融入）
Her mother's calm voice on the phone eased his worries, and he finally allowed himself to sleep. （读后续写·安心）
There was a quiet sense of ease in the little courtyard, where sunlight pooled on the stones and no clock seemed to tick. （读后续写·环境描写）
The champion cleared the final hurdle with ease. 冠军轻松跨过了最后一道栏。

collocations.translation: 自在放松 / 局促不安
collocations.example: She felt at ease with her new classmates, but he was ill at ease in the fancy restaurant. 她和新同学在一起很自在，而他在高档餐厅里却局促不安。

collocations.translation: 缓解压力 / 紧张 / 负担
collocations.example: To ease the burden on overworked students, the school introduced a policy of regular, unstructured free time. （应用文·倡议书）

synonyms.example: A warm meal and a listening ear did much to relieve the weary traveller's despair. （读后续写·温暖）
synonyms.usage: relieve 及物,强调解除痛苦/压力,对象常是具体的负担或情绪;ease 语气更柔和,可指使逐渐、部分地减轻,也能作名词表'轻松'

synonyms.example: She wrapped a blanket around the shivering boy, offering what little comfort she could. （读后续写·关怀）
synonyms.usage: comfort 侧重给予身心的慰藉与安慰;ease 侧重减轻负担或指状态的安适自在,作动词时对象多为 pain/tension

synonyms.example: He spoke three languages with remarkable facility, switching between them without a moment's pause. （议论文·才能）
synonyms.usage: facility(此义)指做事的娴熟、轻松,较书面;with ease 更口语常用,泛指毫不费力

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·ease 三大介词短语（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: with ease 轻松地（= easily） / at ease 自在、舒适（= comfortably；军队稍息） / ill at ease 不自在；put sb at ease 使某人自在
advancedExpressions.example: 老师板书课件三例:I could do it with ease. / I felt completely at ease with my family. / We put Mary at ease by reading her stories. 三个介词短语是高考完形与语法填空高频考点,注意 with ease=方式,at ease=状态。

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. did sth with an ease that ...
advancedExpressions.example: He faced the roaring crowd with an ease that belied the terror pounding in his chest. （with an ease that belied... 表面从容与内心恐惧的反差,续写深化人物）

advancedExpressions.expression: true peace of mind comes not from a life of ease but from ...
advancedExpressions.example: True peace of mind comes not from a life of ease but from the quiet satisfaction of having given one's utmost. （not from...but from... 对照结构，议论文说理）

advancedExpressions.expression: I hope this will go some way towards easing ...
advancedExpressions.example: I hope these arrangements will go some way towards easing the difficulties you have been facing, and please know that our door is always open to you. （安慰信,go some way towards 谦和表达）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The pianist played the difficult part easily.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The pianist glided through the treacherous passage with an ease so complete that the audience quite forgot how many thousands of hours lay buried beneath that effortless grace. （读后续写·举重若轻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: glide through 动态动词 + with an ease so complete that 结果状语 + quite forgot 侧面烘托 + lay buried beneath 隐喻苦练 + 表里对照

sentenceUpgrade.original: I hope this helps to reduce your stress.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I sincerely hope these small gestures will help to ease the weight you have been carrying, and that they remind you, however quietly, that you need not face this alone. （应用文·安慰信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: sincerely hope 诚恳语气 + ease the weight 隐喻负担 + you have been carrying 完成进行体强调持续 + however quietly 插入语柔化 + 情感收束

classPractice.question: 他很聪明，轻而易举地就通过了考试。
classPractice.answer: He was very smart and passed the exam with ease.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题·翻译】考点:with ease = easily"轻而易举地",作方式状语修饰 passed。

classPractice.question: 我给了他一些药以减轻疼痛。
classPractice.answer: I gave him some medicine to ease the pain.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题·翻译】考点:ease 作动词"减轻、缓解",ease the pain"减轻疼痛";to ease... 作目的状语。

classPractice.question: 他尽力表现得轻松自在。
classPractice.answer: He tried his best to appear at ease.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题·翻译】考点:at ease"自在、放松",appear at ease"显得轻松自在",at ease 作表语。

classPractice.question: 选词填空 (with ease / at ease / ill at ease)：The pianist moved through the difficult passage ____, as if the notes cost him no effort at all.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文；with ease = easily 轻松地；at ease 自在，ill at ease 不自在，三者勿混

classPractice.question: I hope these small suggestions will help ____ ____ (ease) the pressure you have been feeling.
